judge_comment: A thermochromic band is a clever passive indicator, but it would respond to the plate rather than the food and microwaves do not heat the zone predictably.

title: Dome Cloche Cooker
new_elements: Dome lid (A microwave dome that lowers over a plate and needs no door, just a lift.)
rationale: A dome placed over a plate is as simple as putting a cover on a dish.
judge_comment: A lift-on dome is an intuitive interaction, but containing microwave leakage without a door and interlock is a serious safety challenge.

title: Wearable Presence Stop
new_elements: Wrist beacon (A wristband that tells the oven when the wearer returns to the kitchen, pausing heating.)
rationale: Pausing when the user is near means the user does not have to remember to stop it.
judge_comment: A wristband adds a device the user must wear and set up, which works against no-learning-curve operation, and auto-pausing on return is odd.

title: Glass Tap-to-Stop Interface
new_elements: Tap-to-stop window (Tapping the window stops the microwave and opens the door in one gesture.)
rationale: One tap on the window handles stopping and opening, which is very easy to remember.
judge_comment: Tap-to-stop is simple, but it only covers stopping and opening, not starting or setting time, and accidental taps are a risk.

title: Cord-Free Sensor Plate
new_elements: Flat sensor plate (A low, flat pad on the counter that replaces the entire control panel.)
rationale: A flat surface with no buttons or knobs is easy to clean and to learn.
judge_comment: A flat sensor plate is feasible, but a buttonless pad doesn't explain how to set time or power, so it may add confusion.

title: Voice-Free Gesture Air Control
new_elements: Hand-wave sensor (A sensor above the door reads an upward wave for more heat and a downward wave for less.)
rationale: Simple hand movements are natural and need no buttons to be found.
judge_comment: Wave gestures avoid buttons, but they are not discoverable without learning and they control only power, not time.

title: Two-Tone Done Pattern
new_elements: Vibrating base alert (The microwave vibrates the counter gently at the end of cooking instead of ringing a bell.)
rationale: A felt vibration is noticed by people who cannot hear the bell.
judge_comment: A vibration alert replaces the bell and helps accessibility, but it does little for the no-learning-curve operation need.

title: Gravity Latch Door
new_elements: Gravity-weighted latch (The door stays closed by weight alone and opens with a gentle pull.)
rationale: No latch to release means nothing to figure out or press.
judge_comment: Replacing the latch with a weighted door is simple, but it conflicts with the safety interlock and sealing requirements.

title: Ambient Glow Done Light
new_elements: Edge-lit casing LED (The outer casing glows a soft color that changes as food finishes.)
rationale: Color conveys status without anyone needing to read or interpret text.
judge_comment: A color glow is easy and clear for status, but it only signals state and does nothing to simplify operating the controls.

title: Turntable-Free Flat Floor
new_elements: Flat ceramic cavity floor (A stationary floor with no tray, easy to wipe clean.)
rationale: Removing a loose part eliminates a common source of confusion and cleaning.
judge_comment: A flat floor without a tray is plausible and removes a loose part, but it is a modest and known change.

title: One-Button Oven
new_elements: Single start button (The only control, which starts the adaptive cycle.)
rationale: With only one control, there is no panel to read or understand.
judge_comment: A one-button microwave is highly plausible and simple, but it is not radical and largely duplicates idea 3.

title: Haptic Done Pulse
new_elements: Door-handle vibrator (The door handle gently vibrates when cooking finishes.)
rationale: The handle tells you when it is done, even from another room of the kitchen.
judge_comment: A vibrating handle is a done alert, which addresses operation only marginally and does little for learning input controls.

title: Swing-Out Pizza Door
new_elements: Bottom-hinged door (The door drops down to form a shelf, holding food at the right height.)
rationale: A door that doubles as a shelf is intuitive and removes a second step.
judge_comment: Drop-down door shelf is plausible and mildly intuitive, but toaster-oven style doors already exist and it doesn't simplify settings.

title: Silicone Curtain Door
new_elements: Flexible silicone curtain (A soft heat-safe curtain that pushes open and springs shut.)
rationale: A curtain you push through needs no handle, latch, or button.
judge_comment: Handle-free push-through curtain is intuitive, but microwave shielding and safety make it very hard.

title: Touch-Plate Starter
new_elements: Food-contact start plate (Touching the food to a plate on the oven starts cooking.)
rationale: Starting by touching the food is direct, so there is nothing to find.
judge_comment: Starting by touching food to a plate is novel and direct, but it is unhygienic and unsafe, and it doesn't say how the cook program is chosen.

title: Liquid Fill Progress
new_elements: Liquid-level progress tube (A coloured liquid rises in a side tube as cooking proceeds and fills at the end.)
rationale: A filling tube is understood by everyone and needs no instructions.
judge_comment: Progress tube is easily understood, but it only shows progress rather than simplifying inputs, and a liquid-filled tube is somewhat awkward to build.

title: Fully Transparent Door
new_elements: ITO-coated transparent conductive glass (A thin indium-tin-oxide coating blocks microwaves while letting visible light through, so the door is clear glass.)
rationale: A fully transparent door means the user simply looks in, with no light to switch on.
judge_comment: Transparent conductive coatings for shielding are plausible and concrete, but the benefit to operating simplicity is marginal because existing mesh doors already let users see in.

title: Ding Vibrates the Handle
new_elements: Haptic door handle (A small vibration motor in the handle pulses when cooking ends.)
rationale: A vibration in the hand is felt even by people who cannot hear or see the signal.
judge_comment: Haptic completion cue is plausible, but it addresses only the end signal, not operation learning, and the user may have already walked away from the handle.

title: Magnetic Latch Door
new_elements: Magnetic detent latch (A strong magnet holds the door closed; a light push releases it.)
rationale: A push-to-open magnet has no lever or hook for anyone to misuse.
judge_comment: A magnetic push-open latch is simple and plausible, but it gives only a modest gain in ease of use and needs safety interlock care.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Sliding drawer door (The front opens by sliding out like a drawer and cuts off the RF when open.)
rationale: A drawer is easy to use at any height and needs no hinge or swing clearance.
judge_comment: A drawer is intuitive and easy to reach, but it does little for operation simplicity, and RF sealing on a sliding drawer is harder than on a hinged door.

title: Lift-Lid Top Opening
new_elements: Gravity-closing lift lid (A top lid lifts up and closes by gravity onto a seal.)
rationale: Lifting a lid is familiar from everyday objects and needs no explanation.
judge_comment: A top lid is familiar from rice cookers and is plausible, but it has no effect on the controls, where the learning curve actually lies.

title: Infrared Surface Finish
new_elements: Infrared surface temperature sensor (An IR sensor reads the surface temperature of the food and stops heating before it boils over.)
rationale: The unit stops before a drink erupts, so the user does not need to know about superheating.
judge_comment: An IR surface sensor to prevent boil-over adds safety but only loosely addresses a no-learning-curve interface, and it adds a component rather than substituting a cheaper one.

title: Wireless Power Base
new_elements: Inductive power base (The unit is powered wirelessly from a flat base.)
rationale: No cable to plug in or trip over, so the unit is ready simply by being placed.
judge_comment: Wireless inductive power is a bold idea that removes setup, but a microwave's kilowatt-level draw makes it very hard and inefficient.

title: Self-Heating Pad Tray
new_elements: Passive thermal-sensing tray (A tray that changes colour when the food is hot enough to eat.)
rationale: A colour change on the plate tells the user when food is safe to eat, with nothing to set.
judge_comment: A colour-change tray gives a simple 'done' cue that fits zero-learning-curve use, though it doesn't replace any component and the name says 'self-heating', which it isn't.

title: Glow-Ring Doneness Indicator
new_elements: Colour-shifting ring light (A ring around the door changes from blue to green as the food finishes.); Show status at a glance (Communicates cooking state without text or sound.)
rationale: A colour change is understood instantly by anyone, with no manual needed.
judge_comment: The colour ring is easy to build but only reports status and does not replace the operating controls, so it does little for the no-learning-curve need.

title: Thermal Camera Mirror
new_elements: Thermal overlay screen (Shows a heat map of the food on the door glass.); Show hot spots (Colours show where the food is hot or cold.)
rationale: A heat map is immediately understood and needs no explanation.
judge_comment: A heat map is intuitive to read, but it only shows state and does not simplify setting up a cook, and it is a costly add-on instead of a substitution.

title: Hot Pan Ring
new_elements: Induction ring (A ring that heats any vessel placed on it, with the vessel's own shape acting as the control.); Heat by vessel (The power is set by the vessel size placed on the ring.)
rationale: Choosing the right bowl sets the power, so no separate setting is needed.
judge_comment: Vessel size setting the power is a clever substitution of the controls, but it is indirect and unreliable, and it is not really a microwave.

title: Inductive Coaster Plate
new_elements: Coaster heater (A flat coaster that heats the bowl set on it, switched on by the bowl itself.); Start on contact (The machine starts when a container touches the surface.)
rationale: Setting the bowl down is the start action, so nothing needs pressing.
judge_comment: Starting on contact removes a step, but induction coasters are not microwaves and auto-starting is unsafe and poorly defined.

title: Self-Stirring Food Cradle
new_elements: Auto-stir cradle (A cradle that rocks food so it heats evenly without a turntable or user stirring.); Heat evenly without action (Even heating happens by itself.)
rationale: Users do not need to know to stop and stir, because the machine does it.
judge_comment: Removes the need to know to stir, but it addresses cooking quality more than operating simplicity, and a rocking cradle is plausible but adds complexity.

title: Vibrating Ready Mug
new_elements: Wearable buzz band (A wristband that buzzes the user when food is ready, across the room.); Signal by vibration (The user is alerted by touch, not sound.)
rationale: A buzz reaches the user wherever they are and needs no understanding of the machine.
judge_comment: A buzz band is easy to build, but it only alerts the user at the end and does nothing to simplify operating the microwave.

title: Two-Zone Ultra-Simple
new_elements: Hot and cold zones (A split interior with a single hot zone that is the only choice.); One choice only (The machine offers only hot or not hot.)
rationale: Offering only one choice removes the need to decide or learn anything.
judge_comment: A single hot/not-hot choice is very simple, but it is not very novel, and the split-zone description is confusing and contradictory.

title: Doorstop Power Gauge
new_elements: Analogue heat gauge (A needle gauge on the door that rises with the heat level.); Read heat as a needle (The user reads the heat as a needle position on a gauge.)
rationale: A needle gauge shows status at a glance and is easy to read without training.
judge_comment: An analogue needle gauge is easy to read and feasible, but it only shows status and does not simplify setting up a cook.

title: Bell-Free Cloud Alert
new_elements: Cloud ping relay (Sends a message to the user's phone when food is ready, using their existing app.); Alert through existing phone (The user hears of completion on a device they already use.)
rationale: Using a device the user already knows means nothing new to learn.
judge_comment: A phone alert is easy to build but adds app setup and doesn't simplify operating the microwave, so it works against the need.

title: Ice-Cube Start Tray
new_elements: Cube-count starter (Starts a program based on the number of cubes or pieces in the tray.); Start by counting (The number of pieces sets the cook time.)
rationale: Counting pieces is a simple physical act that determines cooking time.
judge_comment: Counting pieces to set the time is a novel idea, but reliably sensing item count and mapping it to cook time is hard and imprecise.

title: Glass-Only Touch Surface
new_elements: Feather-touch glass (The glass top responds to a light touch in any place, with no printed buttons.); Touch anywhere to start (Any touch on the glass starts cooking.)
rationale: No button has to be located, because any touch is accepted.
judge_comment: Touch-anywhere start removes button hunting, but ambiguity over time and power and accidental activation undermine usability.

title: Hand-Shaped Heat Control
new_elements: Palm-press heat plate (The user presses a palm onto the plate, and the heat rises with pressure.); Set heat by pressure (Heat level follows how hard the user presses.)
rationale: Pressing harder for more heat is an intuitive action that needs no training.
judge_comment: Pressure-based heat control is intuitive and novel, but a palm on a heated plate raises safety concerns, and holding pressure for the whole cook is impractical and unclear for microwave heating.

title: Top-Loading Drop-In Drawer
new_elements: Top-loading lid (A flip-up lid over the cavity removes the front door and its hinges entirely.)
rationale: Lifting a lid and dropping food in mirrors how people already use a bowl or pot.
judge_comment: A top-loading lid is a radical shift in form and matches the bowl metaphor, but it makes microwave shielding, spills and cleaning harder.

title: Sand-Glass Analog Timer
new_elements: Fill-and-drain sand chamber (A fixed sand chamber drains over the cooking time and ends the cycle when empty.)
rationale: A visible draining sand shows time passing, which is easier to grasp than any digital display.
judge_comment: A sand glass is a simple, intuitive substitute for a digital timer, but a fixed-duration chamber cannot handle varying cook times and users still must choose a time.

title: Haptic Done Mat
new_elements: Vibrating base pad (The base vibrates gently when cooking ends, so users know without hearing a bell.)
rationale: A tactile alert is clear for elderly users who may be hard of hearing.
judge_comment: A vibrating pad is easy to build, but it only changes the alert, not the operation, so it does little for the no-learning-curve need.

title: Spoken Done Announcement
new_elements: Speech synthesis chip (The machine says 'Your food is ready' when cooking ends.)
rationale: A plain spoken message needs no interpretation of sounds or lights.
judge_comment: Voice announcement is easy to implement but only addresses end-of-cycle feedback, not operating the microwave, and it substitutes the beep rather than any control.

title: Tone-Pitch Power Feedback
new_elements: Tone generator (A rising pitch tells the user the power is high; a falling pitch means low.)
rationale: Pitch gives instant feedback on heat level without any visual reading.
judge_comment: Audio pitch feedback is feasible but adds a layer to interpret and does little to simplify operation.

title: Automatic Mains Voltage Sensing
new_elements: Universal auto-ranging power supply (A single supply accepts 100–240 V at 50 or 60 Hz and adjusts itself.)
rationale: One model works everywhere, so users never need to check a voltage label.
judge_comment: Auto-ranging supplies are real, but this is largely irrelevant to operating simplicity for the user.

title: Edge Capacitive Touch Strip
new_elements: Capacitive door-edge strip (A touch strip along the door edge opens the door when touched.)
rationale: A long touch zone is hard to miss and needs no precise pressing.
judge_comment: The touch strip is easy to find but risks accidental openings, and it only addresses door opening, not the rest of the controls.

title: Stationary Stirring Tray
new_elements: Self-stirring tray (A tray with a built-in paddle mixes food so the turntable is no longer needed.)
rationale: Stirring happens automatically, so the user never has to rotate or reposition the food.
judge_comment: A self-stirring tray replaces the turntable and removes the need to reposition food, but it is a mechanical add-on with no direct effect on the learning curve of the controls.

title: Countertop Tile Microwave
new_elements: Flat heating tile (A thin flat panel sits on the counter, heating a plate placed on top.)
rationale: A flat surface needs no door, so there is nothing to open, close or latch.
judge_comment: A flat heating tile removes the door, but it still needs controls and heating without a cavity is slow and unsafe, so it behaves more like a hot plate than a microwave.

title: Sliding Drawer Door
new_elements: Sliding glass drawer front (The door slides sideways on a rail, so nothing needs to swing open or clear space.)
rationale: A drawer motion is intuitive and removes the hinge-swing problem entirely.
judge_comment: A sliding drawer is intuitive, but sealing microwave leakage on a sliding door is harder, and it does not simplify the controls.

title: Thermochromic Doneness Window
new_elements: Thermochromic window film (A film that changes colour when the food reaches a serving temperature.)
rationale: The window visually reveals doneness, so the user does not need to open the door to check.
judge_comment: Thermochromic doneness feedback is clever, but it addresses checking rather than operating, and food temperature sensing through film is questionable.

title: Continuous Power Without Clicks
new_elements: Continuous RF power modulation (Solid-state drive gives smooth power output with no on/off ticking.)
rationale: A power setting then works exactly as it is labelled, with nothing hidden in duty cycles.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already provide continuous power, and it modestly helps by making power settings behave as labelled, though it barely reduces the learning curve.

title: Resettable PTC Fuse
new_elements: Resettable PTC fuse (A self-resetting polymer fuse that trips on overcurrent and recovers after cooling.)
rationale: A fault no longer leaves a dead oven that needs a technician, so the user is never stuck.
judge_comment: Self-resetting fuse is plausible and mildly helpful, but it barely touches the operation-simplicity need and is not radical.

title: Single Hall-Effect Door Sensor
new_elements: Hall-effect door sensor (One magnet and sensor pair confirms the door is shut and cuts power on opening.)
rationale: A simple, always-correct door check removes the need to understand interlock logic.
judge_comment: Hall sensor is feasible, but safety interlocks require redundancy and the user-facing simplicity gain is minimal.

title: Disposable Cook Sleeve Cavity
new_elements: Paper cook sleeve (A microwave-safe sleeve that lines the cavity and is thrown away after each use.)
rationale: Throwing away a sleeve replaces cleaning altogether, which is the simplest possible routine.
judge_comment: A disposable liner is simple and feasible, though it adds waste and addresses cleanup rather than operating the oven.

title: Stackable Modular Cavity
new_elements: Stackable cooking drawers (Shallow stackable drawers each hold a meal and cook one at a time.)
rationale: Each drawer is a single, obvious place for one meal, which suits small kitchens.
judge_comment: Stackable single-meal drawers give an obvious one-meal-one-place mental model and are novel, but they're complex to engineer and not much of a substitution for cost.

title: Switch-Mode Power Supply
new_elements: Switch-mode power supply (High-frequency converter replaces the bulky mains transformer and capacitor.)
rationale: A smaller, lighter power supply makes the oven easier to move and place.
judge_comment: Inverter power supplies are already common in microwaves and have nothing to do with how easy the oven is to use.

title: Halogen Browning Element
new_elements: Halogen radiant browning lamp (A radiant lamp in the lid browns the food surface after microwaving.)
rationale: One setting gives browning, so users get crisp food without choosing a separate mode.
judge_comment: Auto browning cuts mode choices, but halogen-assisted microwaves already exist and it is not a substitution that simplifies operation much.

title: Pre-Printed Food Pad Tray
new_elements: Printed food pad (A disposable pad with printed positioning guides shows where food should sit.)
rationale: Printed guides show users where to place food, so heating is even without any learning.
judge_comment: Printed guides help placement, but they only slightly reduce operation complexity and are not very radical.

title: Sealed Cavity Rapid Steam
new_elements: Pressure-sealed steam bag (A sealed pouch traps steam for faster, even heating of wrapped foods.)
rationale: Sealed bags cook food evenly without stirring, rotating or any setting changes.
judge_comment: A sealed steam pouch can give even heating with no stirring, but pressure-safety concerns and a still-needed time setting limit its simplicity.

title: Cloche Dome Microwave
new_elements: Domed ceramic cloche (Dome lid that sits over a plate and contains the microwaves.); Contains RF with the dome itself (The dome replaces the whole cavity box and door.)
rationale: Lifting a dome from a plate is more intuitive than operating a door.
judge_comment: A dome that replaces the cavity is radical and intuitive, but a ceramic dome can't contain microwaves without a conductive seal, and leakage would be hazardous.

title: Bell to Scent Alert
new_elements: Scent cartridge (Small cartridge that releases a gentle food aroma at the end of cooking.); Signals done by smell (A pleasant smell signals the end without a sound.)
rationale: A smell is an unmistakable 'done' that needs no interpretation.
judge_comment: A scent alert is unusual but only changes the done signal, which was never the hard part of operating a microwave, and cartridges need replacing.

title: Haptic Wristband Alert
new_elements: Haptic wristband (Wearable that vibrates when cooking finishes.); Alerts user wherever they are (Buzzing on the wrist signals completion without a bell.)
rationale: A vibration reaches a student in another room and needs no setting.
judge_comment: A wristband is feasible but adds a device to own and pair, and does nothing to simplify setting up cooking.

title: Battery-Warmed Plate
new_elements: Resistive film heater (Thin film that warms food at low power without RF.); Warming plate (Plate that reheats food slowly.)
rationale: A plate that warms food with no high voltage is the simplest possible heater.
judge_comment: Simple and safe heater, but it replaces the microwave's core function with a slow warmer and doesn't remove operating decisions.

title: Egg-Proof Pressure Cap
new_elements: Pressure-relief cap (Cap that vents steam before eruptive boiling starts.); Prevents eruptions (Vents steam to keep liquids calm.)
rationale: The cap stops eruptions, so the user doesn't need to know about superheating.
judge_comment: A practical safety cap that removes hidden knowledge, but it's a modest, not radical, idea and only tangentially about operation.

title: Shared Oven App-Free Login
new_elements: Proximity badge reader (Reader that recognises the user's phone or card by proximity.); Loads the user's favourite program (Each user's recipe appears when they approach.)
rationale: The oven already knows the user's favourite meal, so the user doesn't have to remember it.
judge_comment: Proximity-based profile loading reduces input steps, but it needs setup and registration, and it is not really a substitution that radically simplifies the microwave.

title: Ring the bell less
new_elements: Haptic wristband alert (A vibration on a watch tells the user the food is ready.)
rationale: Alerts reach the user without any setup beyond wearing the band.
judge_comment: Wristband alert is plausible but addresses notification, not operating the oven, and requires wearing a device.

title: Dial that knows the lunch
new_elements: Meal calendar integration (The oven reads the day's meal plan and offers the next cook.)
rationale: The oven suggests what to cook, so the user does not need to decide the settings.
judge_comment: Calendar-based suggestions reduce decisions but add setup and don't substitute a part; the user must still link a calendar and confirm.

title: Microwave that learns you
new_elements: Habit learning model (Repeated cooks are learned, and the oven starts them with one tap.)
rationale: The machine adapts to the user, so nothing needs to be learned.
judge_comment: Habit learning is plausible but obvious, and it needs initial manual use, so it doesn't fully remove the learning curve.

title: Oven that talks back
new_elements: Conversational assistant (The user asks questions such as 'is it ready' and gets plain answers.)
rationale: Questions replace menus, so the user never has to search for a setting.
judge_comment: Voice assistants on appliances are common and it doesn't substitute a part with something simpler; it adds complexity, though it may reduce menu searching.

title: Shopping-list cooking
new_elements: Grocery order link (The oven reads the item delivered and cooks it when the box arrives.)
rationale: Setup happens before the food is even unpacked.
judge_comment: Zero-interaction cooking is appealing, but it depends on grocery-retailer integration and package identification, and it doesn't really substitute a part.

title: Hot-spot indicator
new_elements: Thermal paint strip (A strip on the plate changes colour when food is evenly hot.)
rationale: The user checks food temperature by glance, with no sensor reading needed.
judge_comment: Thermal paint is a cheap substitute for a sensor, but it indicates doneness rather than simplifying operation and may not survive microwaves.

title: Oven that stops mistakes
new_elements: Metal detector interlock (Stops heating when metal is inside and shows a plain warning.)
rationale: Users are protected from errors they might not know to avoid.
judge_comment: It prevents errors but doesn't simplify operation, and reliable metal detection inside a cavity is tricky; some ovens already have arc detection.

title: Temperature by touch
new_elements: Heat-warning cap (The cap on the food container shows how hot it is through colour.)
rationale: The container tells the user when to stop, so no power setting is needed.
judge_comment: A thermochromic cap is cheap and intuitive, but it doesn't remove the need to set time or power and compatibility is questionable.

title: Air-puff opening
new_elements: Ultrasonic door opener (Waving near the door unlocks it, with no button or handle.)
rationale: Opening the door needs no skill at all.
judge_comment: Touchless opening is easy to use but only covers one step, and the ultrasonic mechanism is vaguely described and replaces a simple handle with something more complex.

title: Sound of food ready
new_elements: Musical done chime (A tune that changes with the food type signals completion.)
rationale: Users know what is done just by the sound, with no reading needed.
judge_comment: A chime that varies by food type is a modest add-on that doesn't simplify operation, and it isn't a substitution of a part.

title: Ask the door
new_elements: Door-mounted display (A small screen on the door shows the food and its status.)
rationale: Status is visible from the door with no need to look inside.
judge_comment: A door screen shows status but adds a component and does little to simplify operation.

title: Shared household memory
new_elements: Family profile swap (Each household member's cooking habits load on their phone's tap.)
rationale: Everyone gets settings that suit them without learning anything new.
judge_comment: Phone-tap profile loading is plausible, but it still requires a phone and doesn't clearly substitute a part; the learning-curve benefit is vague.

title: Crowd-sourced cook guide
new_elements: Community cook library (Popular foods are cooked to proven settings via a shared database.)
rationale: Proven settings are provided automatically, so the user does not need to experiment.
judge_comment: A shared database of settings is feasible but familiar (connected appliances), and it is unclear how the user selects the food without interaction.

title: Phone Is the Control Panel
new_elements: Bluetooth pairing via tap (Phone tap pairs the device and provides the cooking controls.)
rationale: Controls appear on a familiar phone screen, which most people already know how to use.
judge_comment: Phone control is common and adds pairing and app steps, which works against a no-learning-curve goal.

title: Mood Ring Interface
new_elements: Mood-based cook (User states how hungry they are and the device selects the cook.)
rationale: Choosing a feeling is easier than choosing a power level.
judge_comment: Choosing by mood is novel but ambiguous, since hunger does not map clearly to cook parameters, which could add confusion.

title: Dial Hidden Inside Cabinet Wall
new_elements: Retractable control rim (Controls fold away until needed.)
rationale: A clean front shows nothing to be confused by.
judge_comment: Hiding controls gives a clean front but a retractable dial adds a discovery step, so it may increase confusion and is only loosely a substitution.

title: Microwave Reads Your Lips
new_elements: Lip-reading command (Simple mouthed words select the cook.)
rationale: Speaking a single word is the simplest input there is.
judge_comment: Lip-reading is wild and needs no learning in principle, but it is unreliable, needs a camera, raises privacy concerns, and swaps one input for a harder one.

title: Sound of Heat
new_elements: Sound-based status (Each cooking phase produces a distinct sound that anyone recognises.)
rationale: Users learn the cook's stage by ear, not by reading settings.
judge_comment: Audio cues help status comprehension but don't simplify starting or operating, and it isn't really a substitution.

title: Cook by Smell Sensor
new_elements: Gas-sensing cook control (Detects volatile compounds and stops or continues the cook.)
rationale: The machine senses the food directly, removing guesswork from the user.
judge_comment: Auto-cook sensing eliminates user input, but gas sensing is unreliable and similar sensor cooking already exists.

title: Watch the Food Cook on Glass
new_elements: Heads-up projection (Projects cook status onto the glass door.)
rationale: Status is shown exactly where the user is already looking.
judge_comment: Projecting status onto the door is feasible but only modestly helps simplicity, and it substitutes a display rather than simplifying operation.

title: Microwave Tells You Nothing Is Wrong
new_elements: Silent error correction (Device fixes common mistakes such as empty cooking and runs safely.)
rationale: Users are never confronted with error messages they must interpret.
judge_comment: Removing error messages helps, but the fix mechanism is vague and silent correction can mask problems.

title: Cook From Your Pocket
new_elements: Remote heat ping (Phone sends a cook request when the user is on the way home.)
rationale: Food is ready on arrival, so the user never sets anything.
judge_comment: Remote start needs a phone app and someone to load the food beforehand, so it adds complexity and is unsafe.

title: Turn-Table Front
new_elements: Rotating front pivot (The entire front panel pivots sideways on one central post, like a revolving door.)
rationale: A single pivot removes the swing-clearance problem, so the oven can sit close to a wall.
judge_comment: Revolving front panel is radical but awkward for loading food, has sealing challenges, and doesn't clearly reduce learning.

title: Fully Clear Casing
new_elements: Transparent cavity shell (The whole cavity is a sub-wavelength-perforated transparent shell, so the mesh is not needed.)
rationale: Full visibility with no visible grid makes the oven easier to read, and it needs no separate window part.
judge_comment: A transparent perforated cavity shell is novel, but its link to zero-learning-curve operation is weak and containing microwaves that way is doubtful.

title: Universal Voltage Plug
new_elements: Auto-sensing mains converter (Internal converter accepts 100 to 240 V and 50 or 60 Hz without any user setting.)
rationale: No voltage choice is needed, so the user plugs the oven in and it works the first time.
judge_comment: Universal voltage is already common and barely affects operating simplicity, so it serves the need only marginally.

title: Ceiling Light Bar
new_elements: Full-width ceiling light strip (A long, even LED strip across the cavity ceiling lights the whole space evenly.)
rationale: Even light from the top makes the whole cavity easy to see without hot spots or shadows.
judge_comment: Easy to build, but better lighting barely affects ease of operation and is hardly a radical idea.

title: Door-Close-Starts-Cooking
new_elements: Starts cooking on door close (Closing the door begins the last-used heating program.)
rationale: Closing the door is the only action needed, so there is no start button to learn.
judge_comment: Starting on door close is simple, but starting the last-used program unprompted is risky (empty or wrong cook) and safety rules make it hard.

title: Thermochromic Door Heat Map
new_elements: Thermochromic polymer film (Film that changes colour with temperature.); Shows hot zones on door (Colours the door window where food is hottest.)
rationale: Colour signals that anyone can read immediately, so there is nothing to interpret.
judge_comment: Thermochromic film is plausible but shows heat after the fact, so it does little for simple operation, and it's hard to make the door film work in practice.

title: Stop-When-Plate-Is-Lifted
new_elements: Pauses cooking when plate removed (Stops heating if the plate is lifted and resumes when it returns.)
rationale: Removing food is itself the stop action, which removes any need to press stop.
judge_comment: Lifting the plate to stop is intuitive, but a microwave plate is on a rotating turntable and the plate is in a closed cavity, so the stop is already handled by opening the door; the sensing is hard to justify.

title: Magnetic Breakaway Power Plug
new_elements: Magnetic breakaway connector (Magnetic mains connector that pulls apart under a sideways force.); Detaches safely when yanked (Releases the plug without damage or shock risk when pulled.)
rationale: A clumsy tug or a child's pull causes no harm, so nothing needs careful handling.
judge_comment: Magnetic breakaway plugs exist on appliances and add safety, but they do little for learning-free operation.

title: Cordless Battery Reheater
new_elements: Lithium battery pack (Rechargeable pack that powers a small-cavity heater.); Works without a socket (Provides heating anywhere, with no wall outlet needed.)
rationale: Fewer connections mean fewer decisions, and it works in a dorm room without thinking about plugs.
judge_comment: A cordless battery microwave is somewhat bold, but battery power limits are severe and operation itself isn't simplified.

title: Superhydrophobic Self-Clean Cover
new_elements: Superhydrophobic ceramic coating (Coating that repels liquids and food splatter.); Repels splatter (Keeps food from sticking to the cavity wall or cover.)
rationale: No cleaning routine or cover care is needed, so there is nothing to learn.
judge_comment: Plausible and useful for cleaning, but it only loosely addresses operation learning curve and is not very radical.

title: Metamaterial Door Seal
new_elements: Metamaterial RF choke (Engineered surface that blocks microwaves without a rim.)
rationale: A flat seal is easier to wipe clean, so users never need to think about the rim.
judge_comment: Interesting RF choke substitution, but it barely affects how users operate the oven and metamaterial seals are immature.

title: Wall-Mounted Heating Strip
new_elements: Lamp-free heating strip (Flat heating surface that is part of the counter.)
rationale: A flat strip with no cavity and no door has nothing to open or misuse.
judge_comment: Radically simple with no door, but it is no longer a microwave and the safety and heating mechanism are vague.

title: Preheat-Free Boil Ramp
new_elements: Ramps power to prevent superheat (Gradually raises power to avoid sudden eruptive boiling.)
rationale: The machine protects the user from boiling hazards without any caution from them.
judge_comment: A power ramp is a useful safety feature, but it is only loosely tied to simple operation and does not substitute for any control.

title: Chime-Free Haptic Counter
new_elements: Countertop haptic pad (Piezo pad under the counter that gives a gentle buzz.)
rationale: A buzz felt through the counter needs no sound and no interpretation.
judge_comment: A haptic buzz through the counter is a novel completion alert, but it barely helps operation and a microwave isn't always on a pad-friendly surface.

title: Self-Cleaning Cavity Cycle
new_elements: Cleans itself after use (Runs a short steam pulse to loosen residue after each cycle.)
rationale: No cleaning routine is needed, because the machine handles it after every meal.
judge_comment: A steam self-clean is plausible but addresses cleaning rather than operation, and it does not substitute any part.

title: Hand-Shaped Door Pull
new_elements: Fingertip-shaped pull (Ergonomic recess shaped for a fingertip.)
rationale: The shape itself shows how to open the door, so no instructions are needed.
judge_comment: A fingertip recess is easy to build and clear, but it is a minor, obvious tweak that barely affects operation.

title: Hot-Surface Touch Warning
new_elements: Surface warning band (Band that glows red when the outside is hot.)
rationale: A glowing red band warns the user before touching, with no reading required.
judge_comment: Safety cue is intuitive but tangential to operating simplicity and isn't really a substitution.

title: Silent Door Lock Release
new_elements: Electromagnetic latch release (Solenoid release that works without a click.)
rationale: The door opens quietly and smoothly, so the user has no mechanical trick to learn.
judge_comment: A solenoid latch is plausible, but a quiet door barely reduces any learning curve.

title: Induction Charging Base
new_elements: Resonant wireless power (Power crosses a short air gap to a base the oven rests on.)
rationale: Setting the oven on its base is the only connection needed, so there is no plug to find.
judge_comment: Removes the plug, but a microwave needs about 1 kW, so resonant wireless power is inefficient and costly, and the gain in simplicity is small.

title: Infrared Overheat Watch
new_elements: Infrared surface sensor (Measures cavity temperature without contact and cuts power above the limit.)
rationale: Overheat protection works silently, so the user never sees a fault or reset.
judge_comment: An IR sensor is plausible and offers silent safety, but it is only tangentially tied to operation simplicity and is not very radical.

title: Magnetic Fluid Door Seal
new_elements: Ferrofluid seal (A magnetic liquid that seals the gap around the door.)
rationale: The seal stays tight by itself, so the user never needs to check or clean a gasket.
judge_comment: A ferrofluid seal is novel and reduces gasket upkeep, but it is hard to implement, risky near food and heat, and only indirectly serves ease of use.

title: Metamaterial Door Skin
new_elements: Metamaterial RF block (A patterned surface that blocks microwave leakage without a choke.)
rationale: A flat, smooth door is easy to wipe clean and has no groove where food can build up.
judge_comment: A metamaterial door skin is radical and gives a smooth, easy-to-clean surface, but blocking microwaves that way is immature and tangential to learning-free operation.

title: Peel-Off Splatter Film
new_elements: Disposable splatter film (A microwave-clear film that is peeled off and replaced when dirty.)
rationale: Peeling off a dirty film is quicker and easier than cleaning the mica cover.
judge_comment: Eases cleaning but only marginally serves no-learning-curve operation, and the film must be microwave-safe and stay put.

title: Transparent Conductive Window
new_elements: Transparent conductive film (A thin film that is see-through and keeps microwaves in.)
rationale: A clear window that stays cool to the touch is simpler and safer to use.
judge_comment: Conductive film windows already exist as metal mesh and coatings, and the idea does little for operational simplicity.

title: Auto-Discharge on Open
new_elements: Door-triggered discharge (Opening the door connects a bleed path that drains the capacitor.)
rationale: The charge is gone whenever the door opens, so the user never meets a hazard.
judge_comment: Door-triggered bleed discharge is plausible (interlocks and bleeder resistors exist) but it addresses a hazard users never encounter, so it does little for ease of operation.

title: Arc-Warning Cavity Lining
new_elements: Arc-glow liner (A liner that glows red where metal is present and arcing could happen.)
rationale: A visible glow points the user to the metal without any reading or instruction.
judge_comment: A liner that glows near metal is an intuitive visual cue, but the sensing mechanism is unclear and the material is implausible.

title: Thermal Glow Cavity
new_elements: Heat-glow coating (A coating that glows faintly when food is hot, showing the cavity state.)
rationale: The cavity itself gives the status, so no lamp or separate light is needed.
judge_comment: A glowing coating is intuitive status feedback, but it is physically doubtful and potentially unsafe, and the mechanism is vague.

title: Bluetooth Ready Alert
new_elements: Phone alert link (Pairs with a phone automatically and sends a ready message.)
rationale: The user is alerted on a device they already check, so the oven needs no bell or display.
judge_comment: Phone pairing adds setup and a learning curve, which works against simple operation, though the technology is feasible.

title: Kitchen Crowd Mode
new_elements: Shared household profiles (Remembers each person's usual cooking choice and offers it again.)
rationale: The oven remembers habits, so the user repeats one tap rather than learning settings.
judge_comment: Learned habits cut repeated effort, but the first use still needs setup, and the idea is vague and does not replace anything simpler.

title: Hands-Free Door Opener
new_elements: Foot-pedal release (A floor pedal opens the door when a hand is full.)
rationale: The user can open the door with a full plate in hand, with no fiddling with a latch.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is easy to build and concrete, but it addresses door opening rather than learning the operation.

title: Sliding-up door
new_elements: Vertical sliding door (Door rises like a garage door and stays open at any height.)
rationale: A door that moves in a single obvious direction removes any question about how it opens.
judge_comment: A vertical sliding door is mechanically feasible but the learning-curve gain is marginal, and holding it at any height adds complexity.

title: Light-and-haptic done alert
new_elements: Flashing light and pad alert (Flashing light and a vibrating pad signal completion without sound.)
rationale: Several signal channels ensure the done state is noticed by people with weak hearing or sight.
judge_comment: Multi-channel alerts help accessibility but do little for simple operation, which is the core need.

title: Photoluminescent cavity paint
new_elements: Photoluminescent coating (Cavity wall charges from room light and glows, replacing the lamp.)
rationale: The cavity stays visible with zero electricity and no bulb to replace or switch on.
judge_comment: Glow-in-the-dark paint is novel, but it would be dim, and it would degrade under microwave heat and food splatter, so it barely addresses simple operation.

title: Self-cleaning ceramic floor
new_elements: Ceramic floor plate (Non-stick ceramic floor that wipes clean and needs no turntable.)
rationale: A flat ceramic floor is simpler to clean and cheaper than a glass turntable with a drive ring.
judge_comment: A flat ceramic floor is plausible and is used in some units, but it has little effect on learning curve and still has uneven heating.

title: Universal auto-detect plug
new_elements: Auto-voltage power input (Detects 120 V or 230 V mains and adapts without settings.)
rationale: No voltage setting or plug type to choose means one product works everywhere with no setup.
judge_comment: Auto-voltage input is feasible and removes a setup step, but it is rarely relevant to everyday operation and is not very radical.

title: Phased Array Heating
new_elements: Solid-state phased array (Array of emitters that steers energy to every part of the food with no moving parts.); Even heating without rotation (Heats evenly with no rotating plate.)
rationale: With nothing to rotate or reposition, the user has nothing to manage.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF steering is a real technology and a radical substitution for the turntable, but it does little for operational simplicity and is costly.

title: Drawer Cavity
new_elements: Sliding drawer front (Cavity that slides out like a drawer with the food on a fixed tray.); Pull-out loading (Food is loaded by pulling a tray out, not by swinging a door.)
rationale: Pulling out a tray is an obvious movement that needs no instruction.
judge_comment: A drawer is intuitive to use, but sealing microwave leakage around a sliding cavity is hard and the idea doesn't touch the controls.

title: Dishwasher Ceramic Plate
new_elements: Ceramic stoneware plate (Non-stick ceramic plate that lifts out and goes in the dishwasher.); Effortless cleaning (Removes and cleans with no special care.)
rationale: Cleaning needs no special steps, so there is no care routine to learn.
judge_comment: A dishwasher-safe ceramic plate is practical but concerns cleaning, not operation, and is not radical.

title: Shelf Positioning Tray
new_elements: Self-centring tray (Tray that locks into the centre automatically when placed.); Auto-centre placement (Places food in the right spot without the user needing to aim.)
rationale: The tray centres itself, so no positioning is required from the user.
judge_comment: Self-centring is plausible, but it addresses placement rather than operation, so it only marginally serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Stir-Reminder Chime Lamp
new_elements: Gentle nudge lamp (Lamp that brightens and dims to show the food needs stirring.); Stir prompt (Signals that stirring is needed without words.)
rationale: A pulse of light is understood without a sound or message to decode.
judge_comment: Light pulse is simple to build, but the user must learn what the pulse means, and it addresses an edge-case task.

title: Hot Food Haptic Puck
new_elements: Haptic puck (Small puck that buzzes in the hand when the food is ready.); Touch notification (Alerts the user by vibration rather than sound.)
rationale: A buzz in the hand is an unmistakable signal that needs no interpretation.
judge_comment: Haptic alert is novel for a microwave, but a separate puck adds a device to manage, charge and understand, which works against simplicity.

title: Cycle-by-Feel Heat Pad
new_elements: Heat-feel pad (Surface that warms to show roughly how much heat the cycle delivers.); Heat feedback (Shows heat level by feel on the surface.)
rationale: Warmth on the surface shows the setting directly, so no numbers need reading.
judge_comment: Warmth-as-setting is an unusual idea, but a heated surface is unsafe, slow to respond and imprecise, and users would still need to learn how to set the cycle.

title: Self-Lighting Glass Door
new_elements: Electroluminescent door panel (A thin EL layer inside the door glazing gives even light across the window.)
rationale: The door lights its own view, so the user never has to find a light switch.
judge_comment: An EL-lit door is a neat substitute for a lamp, but removing a light switch barely matters because most ovens light automatically.

title: Pod Cavity
new_elements: Disposable microwave pod (A pre-filled, microwave-transparent cup that replaces the cavity as the thing you put food into.)
rationale: The food container is the oven, so loading and cleaning need no instruction.
judge_comment: The idea of a pod replacing the cavity is radical, but it is physically confused (microwaves need a metal cavity), and it does not clearly simplify operation.

title: Door Auto-Latch Magnet
new_elements: Magnetic soft-close latch (Magnets pull the door shut and hold it, so the user just pushes the door closed.)
rationale: Closing is automatic, so the user never needs to check whether the door is sealed.
judge_comment: Soft-close magnetic latches are plausible but mundane, address only door closing, and may conflict with safety interlock requirements.

title: Shelf-Free Cavity
new_elements: Floating flat cavity (A flat, shallow cavity with a single fixed heating area removes all rack and tray choices.)
rationale: A single fixed surface leaves the user nothing to choose.
judge_comment: A single fixed heating surface simplifies choices, but a shallow cavity limits usable space and the description is vague.

title: Redundancy Hidden in Door Hinge
new_elements: Hinge-integrated interlock (The hinge itself carries the switch, so the door cannot be misaligned.)
rationale: The interlock cannot be knocked out of position, so the user does not need to check the door.
judge_comment: A hinge-integrated interlock is a plausible substitution, but safety regulations require redundant interlocks and the benefit to operation simplicity is indirect.

title: Cord-Free Hand Warmer Puck
new_elements: Battery-powered RF puck (A small battery-powered puck heats one mug at a time, with no cord to manage.)
rationale: No cord or socket is needed, so the puck is used the way a mug is used.
judge_comment: A battery RF mug heater is wild but is no longer a microwave and has serious power and safety issues, with only loose ties to the operation need.

title: Magnetic Ring Clasp Door
new_elements: Magnetic hinge pin (A magnetic pivot holds the door open at any angle, with no separate hinge to adjust.)
rationale: A door that stays where it is put removes any wrestling with it.
judge_comment: A magnetic pivot hinge is a clever part substitution but only marginally helps operation simplicity, and the door must stay safely sealed.

title: Glowing Ceramic Cavity Glaze
new_elements: Electroluminescent ceramic glaze (Phosphor-doped glaze inside the cavity lights up when the door opens, with no filament.); Luminous cavity wall (Cavity wall that glows on its own.)
rationale: The cavity is always visible with no bulb to burn out or find.
judge_comment: Self-lighting glaze is inventive, but it barely affects ease of operation and it is doubtful in a microwave cavity.

title: Switching PSU Replaces HV Transformer
new_elements: High-frequency switching power supply (Small SMPS that replaces the bulky mains transformer.)
rationale: Lower cost and less hum, so the appliance feels simpler and cheaper to buy.
judge_comment: Inverter-style power supplies already exist in microwaves, so this is not radical and barely touches the operation-simplicity need.

title: Wireless Induction Base
new_elements: Resonant wireless power transfer (Magnetic resonance coupling from a base to the cooking unit.); Cordless cooking puck (Dish or cavity unit that draws power from a flat base.)
rationale: Dropping the unit on a base means there is no plug, cord, or socket to figure out.
judge_comment: A cordless puck is a bold idea, but plugging in is not a real learning barrier and resonant power at cooking levels is difficult.

title: Polyfuse Self-Reset
new_elements: Resettable polymer PTC fuse (Polymer fuse that resets itself after a fault clears.)
rationale: No one has to find and replace a blown fuse, so the appliance is simpler to recover.
judge_comment: A self-resetting fuse is a plausible, concrete part swap, but it does almost nothing for simple operation or the learning curve.

title: Disposable Cavity Liner
new_elements: Disposable microwave liner (Paper-like liner that lines the cavity and is thrown away.)
rationale: Spills land on a liner that is thrown away, so there is nothing to scrub.
judge_comment: A liner is feasible and lightly reduces cleaning effort, but it does nothing for operation simplicity.

title: Self-Resetting PTC Thermal Cutout
new_elements: PTC thermistor overheat limiter (Self-resetting thermistor replaces both thermal cutouts.)
rationale: Overheating is handled automatically and resets itself, so no one needs to act on it.
judge_comment: A PTC limiter is plausible and concrete, but safety cutouts are invisible to users and it does nothing for operating simplicity.

title: Direct Probe Launch
new_elements: Coaxial probe antenna (Short probe feeds RF straight into the cavity and removes the waveguide duct.)
rationale: A short probe is cheaper and means no metal duct to align or clean.
judge_comment: Plausible engineering substitution, but it does nothing for ease of use and the user would not notice it.

title: Foam Bumper Wrapper
new_elements: Soft foam bumper frame (Padded frame around the cabinet that absorbs knocks and cushions a fall.)
rationale: Soft edges make the appliance safe for children and anyone who is unsteady.
judge_comment: Adds safety and cushioning but does not simplify operation, and it is more an addition than a substitution.

title: Shape-Memory Latch
new_elements: Shape-memory alloy latch (A nitinol wire releases the hook when a small current passes through it, removing the spring lever.)
rationale: Fewer moving parts means fewer ways for the door to jam or confuse the user.
judge_comment: A nitinol latch is a technical swap that the user never notices, so it does little for ease of use, and it still needs a trigger.

title: Projected Food View
new_elements: Top-mounted projector (A small projector shows a live view of the food on the outside of the door.)
rationale: Viewing the food on a surface outside the oven means nobody has to lean in or squint.
judge_comment: A projected view is novel, but it adds complexity and does little for the no-learning-curve need.

title: Wireless Base Power
new_elements: Inductive power base (The microwave sits on a wireless charging base that supplies its power without a cable plug.)
rationale: Setting the appliance on a base with no cable to connect is a simple and quick setup.
judge_comment: Wireless power at 1000+ W is impractical, inefficient and costly, and it does not simplify operation.

title: Tap-Table Oven
new_elements: Table-surface control (The whole top surface is a single touch area that opens the door and starts cooking.)
rationale: Touching anywhere on the top surface does the job, so there are no small controls to misplace.
judge_comment: A whole-surface touch area removes small controls, but opening the door and starting on a stray touch raises accidental-activation and mechanical problems, and the mechanism is vague.

title: Aroma-Cue Finish
new_elements: Scent release vent (A small vent that releases a cooked-food smell when the cycle ends.); Signals cycle completion by smell (Tells the user the food is done by scent, for those who cannot hear a bell.)
rationale: A smell that signals completion works for users who cannot see or hear the bell well.
judge_comment: A scent cue is unusual and accessible, but it does little to simplify operation and a released scent is impractical and may be unappealing.

title: Hinge-Free Flexure Door
new_elements: Flexure door (A door whose front bends at a thin living hinge molded into the polymer frame.); Living-hinge polymer moulding (A thin polymer hinge that flexes many thousands of times.)
rationale: A door with no separate hinge parts has no pinch points and no hinge to get wrong.
judge_comment: A living-hinge door cuts parts, but the user's interaction doesn't change much and polymer fatigue and heat exposure are concerns.

title: Transparent Metamaterial Window
new_elements: Transparent metamaterial pane (A clear pane with a sub-wavelength pattern that blocks microwaves and passes all visible light.); Optically clear metamaterial film (Thin film with a microstructure that is nearly transparent to light.)
rationale: A fully clear window lets users see the food, which removes the need to hunt for a light switch.
judge_comment: Transparent microwave-blocking metamaterial is plausible and novel-ish, but better visibility only weakly serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Glow-Paint Cavity
new_elements: Phosphor-glow cavity wall (Cavity walls coated with a phosphor that glows softly after exposure to light.); Phosphorescent coating (A coating that emits light for a while after light exposure, without any power.)
rationale: The interior stays visible with no bulb to fail or switch, so one fewer thing to operate.
judge_comment: Phosphorescent walls remove a bulb, but the glow would be dim and the benefit to operation simplicity is marginal.

title: Self-Cleaning Liner
new_elements: Disposable cavity sleeve (A microwave-safe liner that is replaced when dirty, not cleaned.); Thermoformed polymer liner (Low-cost moulded liner that lines the cavity.)
rationale: A sleeve you throw away when it is dirty removes all cleaning decisions.
judge_comment: A disposable liner removes cleaning effort but isn't about operation, and has safety and arcing concerns.

title: Pinhole Light Reflector
new_elements: Reflective cavity window (A mirrored sub-wavelength cover that lets the light from the cavity out through reflection.); Metallic sub-wavelength mesh (A dense mesh of sub-wavelength holes that blocks microwaves and transmits light.)
rationale: A window that shows the food with no separate light keeps the interior visible with nothing extra to switch.
judge_comment: Metal mesh windows already exist in microwaves, and the idea does little for operational simplicity; the 'reflective' light-sourcing part is also muddled.

title: Sealed Smell-Sync Panel
new_elements: Single-touch seal (A sealed touch surface on the door with one large open area.); Confirms open state by feedback (Gives a click when the door is closed and a clear change when it is open.)
rationale: Clear click and change feedback make it obvious whether the door is shut without any labels.
judge_comment: Door-state feedback is mildly helpful, but the idea is vague, and the name 'Smell-Sync' doesn't match the description.

title: Thermal Cue Tray
new_elements: Warm-to-touch countertop pad (A warm pad under the microwave that shows when cooking has ended by warmth.); Passive heat-flow indication (A heat-sensitive layer that warms as the unit runs.)
rationale: Feeling warmth under the unit tells the user it is working without reading or listening.
judge_comment: A warm pad is an unusual passive cue, but warmth is a poor and ambiguous indicator, and it could be a safety or heat concern.

title: Sliding Drawer Door
new_elements: Sliding drawer door (Door slides sideways on rails instead of swinging on hinges.); Opens cavity without swing clearance (Slides sideways in a single motion.)
rationale: A drawer-style door is the most familiar mechanism in any kitchen, so it needs no explanation.
judge_comment: A drawer-style door is familiar, but it doesn't simplify operation much and adds sealing and mechanical challenges.

title: Conductive Elastomer Gasket
new_elements: Conductive silicone gasket (Soft gasket with conductive filler seals the door rim.); Conductive elastomer sealing (Silver-filled silicone gives RF shielding.)
rationale: A soft gasket that seals the door on contact removes the precision quarter-wave slot, so it is easier to clean and cannot be mis-assembled.
judge_comment: A conductive gasket is a real engineering substitution, but it is invisible to the user and has little bearing on learning curve.

title: Inductive Pad Base
new_elements: Inductive charging pad (Powers the appliance through a flat pad on the countertop.); Wireless inductive power transfer (Coil-to-coil power transfer over a few millimetres.)
rationale: Placing the appliance on a pad replaces the plug, so there is no cord to route, tangle, or misplug.
judge_comment: Removing the plug is slightly convenient, but the kilowatt-level inductive transfer is challenging and the control interface stays as hard as before.

title: Resettable Polyfuse
new_elements: Resettable polymer PTC fuse (Trips on overcurrent and resets automatically when cool.); Positive-temperature-coefficient polymer (Conductive polymer that resistance-jumps on overload.)
rationale: A fuse that resets itself means the user never has to find, open, or replace a fuse.
judge_comment: Technically plausible, but users rarely interact with fuses, so the effect on operation is marginal and the idea is not radical.

title: Steam Self-Clean Cavity
new_elements: Steam-clean cycle (Water in a tray is heated to loosen grime, which wipes off.); Cleans cavity with one press (Steam cleaning instead of scrubbing.)
rationale: One press cleans the cavity, so no one has to learn how to scrub it.
judge_comment: Feasible and one-press, but it addresses cleaning rather than operating and is already common in ovens.

title: Camera-and-Screen Door
new_elements: Door camera and screen (Tiny camera inside the door shows the food on a screen.); Shows live view of the food (Live picture on the door panel.)
rationale: Seeing the food large on a screen is easier to read than a small glass window in a dim cavity.
judge_comment: A live view makes it easier to see the food, but it adds cost and complexity and does not simplify the controls, which is the main learning barrier.

title: Sand-Filled Timer Chamber
new_elements: Sand timer chamber (Sand drains through a neck to show elapsed time.); Shows elapsed time visually (Sand drain gives a physical countdown.)
rationale: An hourglass needs no electronics, and everyone understands it instantly.
judge_comment: A sand timer is instantly understood and needs no electronics, but it is imprecise, cannot set power or time, and is impractical as the only control.

title: Snap-Fit Roller Ring
new_elements: Snap-fit roller ring (Moulded ring clips to the base with no tools.); Clips in place without tools (Toolless assembly and removal.)
rationale: Toolless removal is simple enough to do without reading anything.
judge_comment: Tool-free roller ring is practical but a minor, obvious tweak that only marginally affects ease of operation.

title: Self-Stowing Cord Reel
new_elements: Retractable cord reel (Spring reel stores the mains cord inside the base.); Stores the cord automatically (No tangled cord on the counter.)
rationale: A cord that stores itself is one less thing for the user to manage.
judge_comment: A retractable cord is feasible but barely relates to operating the microwave without a learning curve.

title: Sand Timer Cook Clock
new_elements: Sand-glass timer window (A visible sand column runs down in step with cooking time.); Passive gravity timing (Time is shown by the physical flow of granules.)
rationale: Remaining time is shown as a visible quantity that anyone can read at a glance.
judge_comment: A visible sand column is intuitive, but a passive sand timer can't accurately track variable cook times and doesn't simplify the actual input.

title: Aroma Done Signal
new_elements: Scent cartridge (Releases a warm toast smell when cooking finishes.); Olfactory done cue (Smell tells the user the food is ready.)
rationale: A pleasant smell replaces an alarm, so there is no sound to interpret.
judge_comment: A scent cue is novel, but cartridges are consumable, smell is an unreliable signal, and it does not help with operating the microwave.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Sliding drawer cavity (Food slides in on a runner, like a drawer, with a pull loop.); Pull-to-load (Loading is done by pulling a drawer, which everyone already knows.)
rationale: A drawer's motion is intuitive and needs no hinge understanding or swing clearance.
judge_comment: A drawer is familiar to use, but sealing the microwave energy around a sliding cavity is hard and it does not address the control interface.

title: Shell Cooking Case
new_elements: Fabric microwave cover (A flexible, shielded fabric that wraps around a bowl.); Flexible EM shielding (Conductive fabric that contains microwaves.)
rationale: A soft wrap with no rigid housing is easier to use, store and understand.
judge_comment: A fabric shield is a radical substitution, but it does little for ease of operation, and containing microwave leakage safely with fabric is doubtful.

title: Doorway Light Bloom
new_elements: Door-edge light strip (A light strip around the door edge brightens when the door opens.); Auto-illuminate on open (Light comes on only when the user needs to see.)
rationale: Light appears on its own when the door opens, so no switch is needed.
judge_comment: Door-triggered lights already exist in microwaves and have little effect on operating simplicity.

title: Mini-Oven Teaching Tray
new_elements: Guided turntable pattern (A printed pattern on the tray shows where to place food.); Placement guidance (Shows the user where to put the food for even heating.)
rationale: A printed guide removes guesswork about where food should go.
judge_comment: A printed placement guide is trivially feasible but only addresses placement, not operation, and is hardly radical or a true substitution.

title: Haptic Power Feedback
new_elements: Vibrating power pulse (The knob pulses in strength to match power, letting users feel the level without looking.)
rationale: Felt feedback removes the need to interpret a visual scale.
judge_comment: Haptic feedback is interesting, but it adds complexity rather than simplifying operation, and it is not a substitution.

title: Sliding Side Door
new_elements: Side-sliding door (The door slides sideways on rails instead of hinging, so it never swings into the user's space.)
rationale: A sliding door is intuitive and cannot be left open by accident.
judge_comment: A sliding door is a mechanical change that is intuitive but not clearly easier to use, and the seal and rail design are problematic for a microwave.

title: Side-Lever Door
new_elements: Full-width grab bar (A large horizontal bar along the door edge; pulling it opens the door.)
rationale: A large bar is easy to grip for users with reduced hand strength or dexterity.
judge_comment: Easy-grip door bar helps accessibility but barely touches the no-learning-curve operation need and is not a radical idea.

title: Transparent Shell
new_elements: Transparent conductive shell (Fine conductive film makes the entire casing see-through while shielding microwaves.)
rationale: A see-through body lets users watch food without any learning or searching for a window.
judge_comment: A see-through body is striking, but it offers little for operating simplicity and fully transparent shielding is a stretch.

title: Sound-Free Doneness
new_elements: Vibration-based stop (A small vibrating pad under the plate pulses when cooking is done, with no audio.)
rationale: Felt completion signals work for users who cannot see or hear the appliance well.
judge_comment: A vibrating pad under the plate is a plausible silent alert but is mostly redundant with idea 1 and tangential to simple operation.

title: Auto Door Unlock by Light
new_elements: Ambient-light door release (The door unlocks when the user holds a light-coded tray card near it.)
rationale: Using the food tray itself to open the door removes the need to find any button.
judge_comment: Light-coded tray card unlocking is odd and adds a new thing to learn, which undermines the no-learning-curve goal.

title: Thermochromic Window Lamp
new_elements: Thermochromic glass coating (Coating that changes colour with temperature so the food's heat is visible through the door.); Shows cooking progress visually (Colour change shows whether the food is hot.)
rationale: A glowing colour is easier to understand than hunting for a light switch or reading a timer.
judge_comment: A thermochromic door is a creative idea, but it is hard to make work inside a microwave door and it does not help with operating the machine.

title: Sliding Glass Door
new_elements: Side-sliding glass panel (A glass door that slides sideways, sealed by a choke gasket.)
rationale: A sliding door never swings into the user's space, so opening it is obvious and never blocked.
judge_comment: A sliding door is somewhat novel, but RF sealing is difficult and it does little for the learning curve.

title: Magnetic Levitating Turntable
new_elements: Magnetic levitation plate (Plate floats on magnets and rotates with a magnetic field, so it has no motor.)
rationale: Removing the motor removes a noisy, failure-prone part the user never needs to think about.
judge_comment: Levitating the plate is wild, but it is expensive and the magnets would have to work inside a microwave cavity; it also barely affects operation.

title: Wireless Power Base
new_elements: Inductive power pad (The microwave sits on a pad in the counter that supplies power without a cord.)
rationale: Setting the oven down is enough to connect it, so there is no plug to find or align.
judge_comment: Removes the cord, but plugging in is not a real learning barrier, so it only marginally serves simple operation.

title: Stove-Top Hob Integration
new_elements: Microwave-in-hob module (A microwave module that sits in a kitchen hob and shares its controls.)
rationale: One set of familiar controls handles both cooking and microwaving.
judge_comment: Sharing familiar hob controls could reduce learning, but the concept is vague and integration of a microwave into a hob raises practical problems.

title: Tray-Free Cook Plate
new_elements: Printed heating film (A flat heating film that replaces the rotating glass plate and needs no motor.)
rationale: There is no tray or motor to get wrong, so the oven is simple to use.
judge_comment: Replacing the turntable with a heating film is a creative substitution, but it barely affects ease of use and does not suit microwave physics.

title: Lamp-Free Transparent Shell
new_elements: Light-guiding acrylic walls (Acrylic walls that carry ambient room light into the cavity.)
rationale: The food is always visible without any switch, so there is nothing to turn on.
judge_comment: Light-guiding walls are inventive, but acrylic is unsuitable and unsafe in a microwave cavity, and the benefit to ease of use is small.

title: One-Button Hot
new_elements: Heat to ready automatically (Heats at a single fixed profile and stops when the food is hot.)
rationale: A single button with one outcome removes the five-step power knob entirely.
judge_comment: One button is very simple, but 'stops when hot' needs a sensor that is never named, and the idea is vague and not very novel.

title: Scent Done Signal
new_elements: Scent cue for completion (A small cartridge releases a popcorn-like smell when cooking finishes.)
rationale: The smell tells the user it is done without any beep or number to interpret.
judge_comment: A scent cartridge is novel, but it needs consumables, may not be wanted, and does not make operating the microwave any simpler.

title: Haptic Tray Pulse
new_elements: Vibrating tray buzzer (The turntable vibrates gently to signal the end of cooking.)
rationale: A physical nudge replaces the bell, so the signal works even for users who cannot hear well.
judge_comment: A vibrating turntable is a plausible alert, but vibration can disturb food and the alert only concerns completion, not operation.

title: Lamp-Free Clear Cavity
new_elements: Transparent conductive cavity wall (A clear coating lets light from outside show the food without a bulb inside.)
rationale: The food is visible with no lamp to switch on or explain.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive cavity wall is inventive, but containing microwaves while letting enough light in is difficult, and it barely affects the learning curve.

title: Auto-Discharge Bleeder
new_elements: Passive bleeder resistor (A resistor drains the capacitor within seconds of switch-off.)
rationale: The unit is safe to touch immediately, so no wait-and-check routine has to be learned.
judge_comment: Bleeder resistors are already standard in microwaves, and the benefit has little to do with ease of use.

title: Sand Timer Tray
new_elements: Physical sand-glass timer (A sand-glass runs as the food cooks, and empty means done.)
rationale: Watching sand fall is self-explanatory, so no digits or dials need interpretation.
judge_comment: A sand-glass is simple to read but must be calibrated to the cook time, so the user still has to decide how long to cook and it adds little.

title: Flip-Up Lid Door
new_elements: Top-hinged lid (A lid lifts like a bread box and needs no latch or hook.)
rationale: A lid that lifts with a finger has no mechanism to understand.
judge_comment: A lid is simple to open but does little for operation overall, and a top-hinged door causes microwave-seal and safety problems.

title: Gravity Hatch
new_elements: Self-closing gravity hatch (A heavy hatch closes by gravity and seals the cavity.)
rationale: Closing happens on its own, so the user never has to check whether the door is sealed.
judge_comment: A self-closing door removes one small step, but a microwave door must latch with interlocks, so it only modestly simplifies operation and is hardly radical.

title: Ceramic Self-Clean Cover
new_elements: Glazed ceramic splatter cover (A glazed ceramic cover resists sticking and wipes clean in one pass.)
rationale: A surface that wipes clean with no scrubbing means no cleaning routine to learn.
judge_comment: A ceramic cover is feasible and easy to wipe, but it concerns cleaning rather than learning how to operate the appliance.

title: Wipe-Clean Silicone Liner
new_elements: Disposable microwave liner (A printed liner sits on the floor and is replaced when dirty.)
rationale: Replacing a liner is simpler than knowing how to clean the cavity.
judge_comment: A disposable liner is plausible and simple, but it addresses cleaning rather than operation and is not very radical.

title: Sleep-Off Auto Power
new_elements: Auto power-down (The oven shuts down fully when not in use and needs no switch.)
rationale: No on or off switch exists to remember or misuse.
judge_comment: Auto power-down removes an on/off step, but microwaves already have standby and the idea does not simplify actual operation.

title: Pet-Free Plug Chime
new_elements: Plug-in status plate (A small coloured plate on the power cord that lights up when the machine is powered.); Power readiness (Shows the machine is ready to use.)
rationale: A simple readiness signal removes the question of whether the machine is on.
judge_comment: A cord power indicator is trivial and has little to do with learning to operate a microwave; the name also mentions a chime and pets, which the idea doesn't use.

title: Parent-Proof Pause Latch
new_elements: Magnetic door lock (Magnetic catch that keeps the door shut during cooking and releases only at the end.); Automatic safety lock (The door locks and unlocks with no user step.)
rationale: Safety happens without any action from the user, so no child-lock setting needs learning.
judge_comment: Auto-locking door is plausible and removes the child-lock step, but it addresses only a minor part of operation simplicity and is not radical.

title: Recipe Projection on Ceiling
new_elements: Overhead projector (Shows picture-based steps above the machine, such as 'stir' or 'wait'.); Guided steps (Shows the next step in plain images.)
rationale: Step-by-step pictures guide the user through a recipe with no reading.
judge_comment: Pictorial projected steps are novel but add a complex feature and mostly help recipes rather than simple everyday operation.

title: Cook Pyramid Stack
new_elements: Stacked cook tiers (Stackable pieces that set the level of cooking according to height.); Height-based power (The height of stacking sets the power.)
rationale: Stacking is a physical act that a child could do, so the setting is intuitive.
judge_comment: Stacking height setting power is playful, but it adds objects to manage and is not obviously simpler than a dial, and the mechanism is unclear.

title: Induction Pad Power Base
new_elements: Inductive power pad (Oven sits on a flat pad that powers it through the base, so no plug is ever inserted.)
rationale: Setting it down on the pad is the only action needed to power it on.
judge_comment: Wireless power at microwave-oven wattage is impractical, and it does not address the cooking settings that cause the learning curve.

title: Silent Countertop Pulse
new_elements: Tabletop light pulse (Light pulses through the counter surface to indicate the end of cooking.)
rationale: Silent, glanceable signalling works in shared flats where a bell annoys people.
judge_comment: Light through a countertop is a silent, glanceable cue, but the mechanism is vague and it is only mildly relevant to ease of operation.

title: Fridge-Style Drawer Door
new_elements: Sliding drawer front (Door slides out sideways like a drawer, with no hinge or latch to find.)
rationale: Anyone who can open a drawer can open this, with no hook or button to learn.
judge_comment: A drawer door is intuitive, but microwave sealing and safety interlocks make a sideways-sliding door hard.

title: Disposable Splash Film
new_elements: Peel-off splash film (Cheap disposable film covers the inside and peels off each week.)
rationale: Replacing mica cleaning with peel-off film removes scrubbing from the user's routine.
judge_comment: It reduces cleaning effort but does little for operating simplicity, and film in a microwave cavity raises safety and arcing concerns.

title: Dishwasher Plate Set
new_elements: Dishwasher-safe turntable (Turntable made of unbreakable polymer that fits the dishwasher.)
rationale: Cleaning is done by the dishwasher, so the user does not have to handle the plate.
judge_comment: A dishwasher-safe polymer plate is practical, but it is an obvious change and has only a marginal bearing on operational simplicity.

title: Hot-Swap Cassette
new_elements: Sealed magnetron cartridge (Sealed RF cartridge that is swapped as a unit when it fails.)
rationale: Users never open the casing, so fixing a fault is a cartridge swap, not a repair.
judge_comment: A swappable sealed cartridge is about repair, not operation, so it hardly serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Scent Chime
new_elements: Scent cartridge release (Releases a faint food smell when cooking finishes); Signals completion by smell (Tells the user the food is ready without sound)
