judge_comment: A fully glass cavity doesn't address operation and is problematic for microwave shielding, so it is weakly related to the need.

title: Stackable Cube Oven
new_elements: Modular stacking unit (Cube modules stack and lock together, each a single fixed function with no hinge.)
rationale: A cube with one function is easy to understand and can be placed anywhere without setup.
judge_comment: Stackable single-function cubes are intriguing but unclear how they simplify operation, and a hinge-free design raises practical questions about access.

title: Stamped Steel Simplicity
new_elements: One-piece stamped cavity (The cavity and hinge are one stamped piece, with no separate hinge fitting.)
rationale: Fewer parts means fewer ways for the oven to be misused or to fail in the user's hands.
judge_comment: This is a manufacturing simplification with no visible effect on how users operate the oven, so it barely serves the need.

title: Sound-Free Glass Door
new_elements: Laminated glass shield (A laminated glass pane replaces the mesh window and blocks microwaves through its conductive film.)
rationale: A clear glass door looks safe and simple, so the user trusts it without any warning labels.
judge_comment: Laminated glass with conductive film is plausible, but it mainly changes the look and does little for operation simplicity; the 'sound-free' name is also unclear.

title: Single Solid-State Interlock
new_elements: Watchdog safety chip (One chip monitors the door and shuts down the power circuit when needed.)
rationale: A single chip is simpler to make and to understand than three switches in series.
judge_comment: An internal safety chip is invisible to the user, so it does nothing for the learning curve, and it still needs redundancy to be safe.

title: Moulded conductive-polymer shell
new_elements: Conductive polymer moulding (Polymer shell with conductive filler replaces stamped steel.)
rationale: A single moulded shell has no seams or dents to confuse or hurt users, and is cheaper to make.
judge_comment: A conductive polymer shell is unusual, but it does not address operation, and microwave containment and safety make it very hard to achieve.

title: Snap-fit flatpack casing
new_elements: Snap-fit casing (Casing snaps together with no fasteners or welds.)
rationale: Simple assembly cuts cost while keeping the product easy for any user to understand.
judge_comment: Snap-fit assembly is a manufacturing saving with no bearing on how the user operates the microwave, and RF sealing and structural strength are concerns.

title: Light Pipe from the Room
new_elements: Fibre light pipe (A clear acrylic light guide carries room light through the door window into the cavity.); Total internal reflection light guiding (Light stays inside a polymer rod and exits at the far end.)
rationale: The cavity stays visible with no bulb to replace, so there is nothing to maintain.
judge_comment: A passive light pipe replaces a bulb, but room light entering through the door would be too dim and it does little for ease of operation.

title: Auto-Discharge Capacitor Dock
new_elements: Dock-triggered HV discharge (Removing the oven from its dock fires a discharge path, so the cavity is safe to touch at once.)
rationale: The hazard is removed by the same act that disconnects the oven, so the user has nothing to remember.
judge_comment: Automatic discharge on undocking is interesting for safety, but it has little to do with operation simplicity and would be tricky to implement.

title: Built-In Cabinet Insert
new_elements: Under-cabinet drop-in module (Installed flush in a cabinet, it is operated through the cabinet door.)
rationale: A built-in unit sits at a natural height, so there is no reaching or bending.
judge_comment: Built-in microwaves already exist and the idea substitutes nothing, while operating through a cabinet door adds complexity and does little for learning curve.

title: Magnetic Levitation Tray
new_elements: Magnetic levitation tray support (Tray floats on magnets with a rotating field, so no roller ring is needed.)
rationale: No rollers or ring to catch crumbs or clean, so there is nothing to maintain.
judge_comment: Levitating the tray is impractical in a microwave cavity and only helps cleaning, not ease of operation.

title: Single Magnetic Reed Interlock
new_elements: Magnetic reed door sensor (One reed switch and magnet in the door frame replace the three switches.)
rationale: A simpler door sensor reduces the parts needed and removes a confusing cluster of switches.
judge_comment: A reed switch replacing the interlocks is plausible, but safety standards require redundant interlocks, and users see no operational simplification.

title: Shielded Cord Replaces EMI Block
new_elements: Shielded integral cord (Mains cord with built-in ferrite shielding replaces the filter block.)
rationale: Fewer separate parts means lower cost and no extra box to fit in the cabinet.
judge_comment: A shielded cord replacing the EMI filter is a cost-cutting part swap that is unlikely to work well and has no bearing on ease of use.

title: Current-Limit GaN Driver
new_elements: Digital current limiter (Electronic limit replaces the ceramic fuse and thermal cutout with one chip.)
rationale: One chip protects the appliance with no fuse to replace and no separate cutout to test.
judge_comment: This is an internal safety substitution the user never sees, and an electronic limiter cannot fully replace a thermal cutout for safety compliance.

title: Glowing Cavity Wall
new_elements: Phosphor-coated cavity wall (The cavity wall is coated with a phosphor that glows after a flash of light from the front LED.)
rationale: The inside stays visible without an extra lamp, so there are fewer parts to fail.
judge_comment: A phosphor coating would be a radical substitution, but afterglow is dim, cavity coatings face heat, grease and microwaves, and it has little to do with learning curve.

title: Paper-Pulp Cavity
new_elements: Moulded fibre cavity (A microwave-shielded cavity made from moulded fibre with a metal-coated lining.)
rationale: A recyclable fibre cavity is light, cheap and easy to replace if damaged.
judge_comment: A fibre cavity is radical but unsafe, since it risks fire and arcing, and it has no link to ease of operation.

title: Silicone Ring Tray
new_elements: Silicone turntable ring (A flexible silicone ring replaces the glass turntable and cannot shatter.)
rationale: A flexible tray cannot crack from a knock, which removes a common reason to call for help.
judge_comment: A silicone tray substitutes for glass, but shatter-proofing barely affects operational simplicity, and silicone's heat tolerance and rigidity for rotation are questionable.

title: Self-Cleaning Cavity
new_elements: Non-stick cavity coating (A cavity coating that food cannot stick to, so there is no need to wipe it clean.)
rationale: Nothing needs cleaning or scrubbing, which removes a confusing maintenance task.
judge_comment: A non-stick coating reduces cleaning effort but does little for operating the microwave, and the claim that no wiping is needed is optimistic.

title: Hot-Air Warning Shell
new_elements: Cool-touch outer skin (A cool-to-touch outer layer keeps the outside safe to hold even during cooking.)
rationale: An outside that stays cool means the user cannot be burnt by a mistaken touch.
judge_comment: A cool-touch exterior improves safety but does little for operation without a learning curve.

title: Snap-Fit Shell
new_elements: Tool-free snap-fit assembly (Parts clip together without welding, screws or tools.); Snap-fit housing (A housing made from snap-fit moulded panels.)
rationale: Snap-fit parts make the product cheaper to build, so the simple design can sell at a lower price.
judge_comment: Snap-fit housing lowers manufacturing cost but does not address operational simplicity for users.

title: Thermoplastic Body
new_elements: Moulded composite body (A body moulded from recycled composite with a metallised RF shield.); Metallised plastic shielding (A metal-coated plastic shell that blocks microwave leakage.)
rationale: A cheaper plastic body with a metal coating lowers the price so more people can afford the simple unit.
judge_comment: Cost-focused body swap does little for no-learning-curve operation, and metallised plastic shielding is plausible but not radical.

title: Single Thermistor Safety
new_elements: Dual-zone NTC thermistor (One thermistor monitors magnetron and cavity temperatures.); Monitors cavity and magnetron temperature (Cuts power on overheat.)
rationale: One sensor covers both overheat risks, which means fewer parts to fail and fewer ways for a user to be confused.
judge_comment: This is an internal cost-saving change that users never see, so it does little for simple operation.

title: Heat-Pipe Silent Cooling
new_elements: Copper heat pipe (Sealed pipe carries heat from the magnetron to external fins.); Two-phase heat-pipe transport (Passive evaporation and condensation transfers heat.)
rationale: With no fan to switch on or hear, the appliance simply works and stays quiet.
judge_comment: Silent passive cooling is mostly irrelevant to operational simplicity, since users already don't operate the fan, and heat pipes alone are likely insufficient for magnetron loads.

title: Piezo Fan
new_elements: Piezoelectric air blade (Vibrating ceramic blade moves air with no motor.); Piezoelectric actuation (Ceramic deforms with applied voltage.)
rationale: A motorless fan has no moving parts to wear out or need maintenance.
judge_comment: A piezo fan is a component swap that does not change the user's operation, and its airflow is likely too weak for magnetron cooling.

title: Ferrite Bead EMI Filter
new_elements: Ferrite bead on mains lead (Single ferrite bead suppresses conducted noise.); Ferrite noise suppression (Ferrite absorbs high-frequency noise.)
rationale: A single bead replaces a full filter block, which is simpler to build and to repair.
judge_comment: Ferrite beads are already standard practice and have no bearing on how simple the microwave is to operate.

title: Metallised Plastic Cavity
new_elements: Metallised plastic cavity (Injection-moulded plastic with conductive metal coating.); Conductive plating on polymers (Metal layer on molded plastic.)
rationale: A lightweight plastic cavity is cheaper to make and easier to lift and clean.
judge_comment: A metallised plastic cavity may cut cost and weight, but it has no effect on ease of operation, and it raises arcing and heat-durability problems.

title: Coaxial Feed replaces Waveguide
new_elements: Coaxial feed probe (Coax line carries RF from magnetron to cavity.); Coaxial TEM transmission (Simpler transmission mode than TE10.)
rationale: A simple coaxial feed is easier to make and fit, which keeps the appliance affordable.
judge_comment: A coaxial feed is an internal RF change that does nothing for operational simplicity and has real power-handling challenges.

title: Printed-Polymer Cavity
new_elements: Injection-molded microwave-safe polymer cavity (The steel cavity and wrapper are replaced by a molded polymer shell with a conductive coating.)
rationale: A lighter, cheaper body makes a simple appliance even more affordable for the entry segment.
judge_comment: A cheaper body doesn't address operation simplicity, and a polymer cavity with conductive coating has serious arcing and heat problems.

title: Self-Discharging Electronics
new_elements: Passive shorting bleed circuit (A spring-loaded short drains all stored charge the moment the door opens.)
rationale: No user action is needed to make the machine safe to touch after use.
judge_comment: Microwaves already have bleeder resistors and door interlocks, and safe discharge does little for learning-curve-free operation.

title: Self-Cleaning Pyrolytic Cavity
new_elements: Burns off food residue (A high-temperature cycle clears spills automatically.)
rationale: Cleaning is one button press, so there is no scrubbing to figure out.
judge_comment: One-button cleaning is simple, but it targets maintenance not operation, and pyrolytic temperatures are impractical for microwave cavities and parts.

title: Bimetal-Free Overheat Guard
new_elements: Software thermal model (Estimates the safe limit from power use and time.)
rationale: Overheating is prevented silently, so the user never sees a fault.
judge_comment: A software overheat guard replaces a bimetal part plausibly, but it is invisible to the user and does almost nothing for operational simplicity.

title: Fridge-Door Oven Mode
new_elements: Fridge-integrated microwave drawer (A microwave drawer built into the fridge door, sharing one interface.)
rationale: Food goes from fridge to oven in one motion with a single set of controls.
judge_comment: Integrating the microwave into the fridge door is a novel form factor, but it doesn't clearly reduce learning, and the SUBSTITUTE operator isn't evident.

title: Liquid Metal Seal
new_elements: Self-healing liquid metal gasket (A gallium alloy seal reforms itself after damage and seals the gap.)
rationale: A seal that repairs itself removes the need for any user maintenance.
judge_comment: A liquid gallium seal is novel, but it is unsafe and impractical for microwave leakage, and it barely affects operational simplicity.

title: Self-Regulating PTC Heater
new_elements: PTC self-limiting element (Ceramic element that limits its own temperature without a switch.)
rationale: No thermostat means no trip-out to diagnose or reset.
judge_comment: A PTC heater is unrelated to a microwave's magnetron operation and has little effect on user learning.

title: Self-Cleaning Plasma Walls
new_elements: Catalytic wall coating (Walls coated to break down grease and splatter during cooking.)
rationale: The oven cleans itself, so the user never needs a cleaning procedure.
judge_comment: Self-cleaning is a nice benefit but is only tangentially about operation, and catalytic coatings are known from ovens; the 'plasma' label is vague and inaccurate.

title: Ceramic Floating Plate
new_elements: Ceramic floating plate (Ceramic plate floats on air jets and needs no glass or motor.)
rationale: A plate that floats is one part with no drive mechanism to wear out.
judge_comment: Air-jet levitation is wild but implausible in a microwave cavity, is more complex than what it replaces, and does little for ease of operation.

title: Dishwasher Silicone Tray
new_elements: Flexible silicone tray (Soft tray that is dishwasher safe and never cracks)
rationale: The tray is hard to break and simple to clean.
judge_comment: Silicone tray in a microwave is plausible, but it targets durability and cleaning rather than learning-free operation, and it is not radical.

title: Single-Piece Moulded Housing
new_elements: Single-shot moulded shell (One moulded piece replaces stamped sheet and many screws)
rationale: Fewer parts make the machine easier to understand and to fix.
judge_comment: A single moulded housing is a manufacturing and cost change that does not affect how the user operates the product.

title: Bioluminescent Cavity
new_elements: Electroluminescent cavity wall (A thin film on the inner wall glows softly, visible through the door with no bulb.)
rationale: The light is part of the walls, so there is no bulb to replace and no switch to find.
judge_comment: An electroluminescent film inside a microwave cavity is impractical and does little for ease of operation.

title: Transparent Sealed Pod
new_elements: Clear sealed cooking pod (A fully transparent heating pod that shows the food from any angle.)
rationale: Seeing food clearly from all sides removes the need to open the door to check.
judge_comment: Visibility helps monitoring but doesn't simplify operation, and a fully transparent pod is hard to make with microwave shielding.

title: Stamped Metal Replaced By Molded Shell
new_elements: Molded recycled shell (Shell is moulded from recycled fibre and polymer instead of stamped steel.)
rationale: A lighter, cheaper shell keeps the oven affordable and easy to lift for any student.
judge_comment: A molded shell is a cost and weight change; it also fails RF shielding needs and does nothing for ease of operation.

title: Foam Chassis Oven
new_elements: Foam-moulded chassis (Interior chassis is a single moulded foam part with snap fit wiring channels.)
rationale: Fewer parts make assembly cheaper and mean fewer things to go wrong for the user.
judge_comment: Foam near a magnetron is questionable for heat and fire safety, and the link to a no-learning-curve interface is tenuous.

title: Moulded conductive polymer cavity
new_elements: Conductive-coated polymer moulding (Injection-moulded polymer with a conductive metallic coating replaces stamped steel.)
rationale: A cheaper shape lets the product stay low cost, which keeps simple machines available to elderly buyers.
judge_comment: A moulded conductive cavity is a cost substitution with no direct bearing on ease of operation, and it is questionable for RF containment and heat.

title: Low-Voltage Battery Pack Base
new_elements: Docking battery base (A rechargeable base powers the unit in short bursts, plugged in and charged overnight.)
rationale: A single base with no cord means no plugging-in mistakes and no regional voltage confusion.
judge_comment: A battery base for a roughly 1kW microwave is impractical, and charging adds a new step that works against simplicity.

title: Ceramic Fuse-Free Cutoff
new_elements: Smart integrated protection chip (One chip handles overcurrent and overheat protection and shows a single status light.)
rationale: One unit that protects everything means nothing needs checking by the user.
judge_comment: A single protection chip with a status light is vague, and the user is rarely involved in protection anyway.

title: Open Air Cooker Bowl
new_elements: Bowl-mounted sensor (A sensor on the bowl rim that tracks the food's temperature and signals in the bowl.)
rationale: The signal comes from the bowl itself, so no timer or bell is needed on the oven.
judge_comment: A bowl-mounted sensor is hard to make microwave-safe and the 'open air' framing is unclear; it adds a device rather than simplifying.

title: Absorbing Gasket Seal
new_elements: RF-absorbing silicone gasket (A lossy silicone gasket soaks up leakage at the door rim without a precision slot.)
rationale: A simple soft gasket replaces a precision slot, so the door looks and feels like an ordinary seal.
judge_comment: An absorbing gasket is an internal safety detail the user never perceives, so it does little for learning-free operation, and it is probably insufficient alone for leakage control.

title: Molded Polymer Shell
new_elements: Single-piece moulded shell (A moulded outer shell replaces the stamped steel wrapper and is shielded inside.)
rationale: A smooth, light shell has no edges to catch on, so the appliance is intuitive to move and handle.
judge_comment: A shielded polymer shell is plausible but has heat and shielding challenges, and it barely relates to operating simplicity.

title: Photoluminescent Glow Cavity
new_elements: Photoluminescent cavity paint (Stores light from the room and glows without power or heat.)
rationale: The cavity stays visible for food checking with no bulb to switch on or manage.
judge_comment: Glow paint is a real substitute for a bulb but barely relates to operation simplicity, and it would be too dim and is not heat-proof.

title: Battery Pack Oven
new_elements: Swappable battery pack (Rechargeable pack powers the RF stage.)
rationale: With no cord or outlet to find, the machine can sit anywhere without setup.
judge_comment: Microwave power draw is too high for a practical battery, and it adds charging and swapping chores instead of removing them.

title: Silent Peltier Cooling
new_elements: Peltier cooling plate (A solid-state cooler removes heat from the electronics with no fan.)
rationale: A silent oven that does not hum or whir is calmer for a student sharing a flat.
judge_comment: Silent cooling has little to do with a no-learning-curve operation, and Peltier modules are inefficient and costly for this use.

title: Always-Ready Standby
new_elements: Instant reheat on touch (Stays warm in standby so any food placed in it heats without any setting.)
rationale: Constant readiness means the user never has to start or set anything.
judge_comment: Removing settings is appealing, but a warm standby that heats any food automatically is vague, energy-wasteful and risks overcooking or being unsafe.

title: Soft-start software filter
new_elements: Soft-start RF ramp control (Ramps the magnetron on gently to cut conducted noise, with no bulky filter.)
rationale: Smooth power ramping reduces noise and cost without the user having to know anything about it.
judge_comment: Soft-start ramping mainly addresses EMI and cost, which is invisible to the user and does nothing for operational simplicity.

title: Modular stackable cavities
new_elements: Stackable cavity modules (Interlocking cavity blocks that stack or add a level without tools.)
rationale: Adding space by stacking is obvious and needs no setup.
judge_comment: Stackable cavities add complexity and RF/power-feed problems, and claim of 'no setup' is dubious; weakly tied to simple operation.

title: Louvre-less door-seam venting
new_elements: Door-seam vent path (Air leaves through a controlled seam at the door, with no louvres on the body.)
rationale: A clean body with no vent grille can be placed closer to walls, which suits small kitchens.
judge_comment: Door-seam venting aids placement rather than operation, and controlling leakage and heat at the seam is difficult.

title: Stackable Modular Oven Block
new_elements: Snap-together microwave module (A single block with one door and no visible hardware beyond a front slot.)
rationale: A single-slot block has fewer parts to understand and no separate controls to find.
judge_comment: A single-slot block with no controls is vague about how it is operated and does not clearly serve a no-learning-curve need.

title: Living-Hinge Molded Polymer Door
new_elements: Injection-molded living hinge (Polymer hinge molded in one piece with the door frame.)
rationale: A one-piece hinge has no separate parts to fail or confuse, and it costs less to make.
judge_comment: A living hinge cuts cost but does nothing for ease of use, and it is questionable for a heavy door that must hold up to heat.

title: Battery Buffer for Quick Heat
new_elements: Supercapacitor energy buffer (Stored energy lets the oven run on short bursts from a modest socket)
rationale: Buffered power lets a small plug work, so the user does not need a special circuit or outlet.
judge_comment: Supercapacitor buffering for a modest socket does not address operational simplicity, and it is an expensive substitution with limited energy for a microwave's kW load.

title: Look-Through Sealed Door Glass
new_elements: Solid glass door panel (Full-size tempered glass panel with conductive coating and no holes)
rationale: A clean, unbroken window is easy to read and easy to wipe down.
judge_comment: A solid glass door with conductive coating is plausible, but it doesn't clearly reduce the learning curve and most microwaves already use a mesh-based window.

title: Glowing Feel-Good Light
new_elements: Mood-cook lighting (Cavity lighting shifts to warm tones that make reheating feel comforting)
rationale: A warm, inviting light turns a simple reheat into a pleasant moment, with no controls to learn.
judge_comment: Mood lighting is pleasant but does not make the microwave easier to operate.

title: Sealed Cavity Chamber
new_elements: Metal-free sealed cavity (A sealed chamber with a microwave-safe liner stops objects from being put in the wrong way.)
rationale: A cavity that rejects metal by design removes a common mistake the user would otherwise have to remember.
judge_comment: Preventing misuse is relevant to simple operation, but a sealed cavity that rejects metal is vague, and the mechanism is unclear and impractical for loading food.

title: Passive Chimney Cooling
new_elements: Passive heat-pipe chimney (A heat pipe carries heat out through a rear fin with no fan.)
rationale: With no fan there is no noise and no fan to clean, so the unit is calm and quiet.
judge_comment: A passive heat-pipe chimney is a real mechanism, but it barely touches operational simplicity and likely can't cool a magnetron adequately without a fan.

title: Silent Cooling Fan
new_elements: Brushless thermally controlled fan (A quiet fan that only runs when needed.)
rationale: A quiet unit feels less alarming and needs no attention.
judge_comment: A quiet thermally controlled fan is a routine component and has little connection to learning-free operation.

title: Cord-Free Carry Handle
new_elements: Built-in carry handle with cable reel (A top handle hides a cable reel and locks the door during carrying.)
rationale: The unit can be carried and stored without loose cables to manage.
judge_comment: A cable reel and carry handle help portability, not simplicity of operation.

title: Fire-Safe Heat Shield
new_elements: Intumescent vent shield (A vent shield swells to block the vent if the unit overheats.)
rationale: A fail-safe shield protects the household without requiring the user to act.
judge_comment: Intumescent vent shield is a safety feature, not simple operation, and it's hardly a substitution; the swelling mechanism is only loosely plausible.

title: Mirror-Surface Oven Wall
new_elements: Reflective cavity (A mirrored cavity that shows the food from all sides through reflection.); See all sides by reflection (Food is seen from several angles with no moving parts.)
rationale: Reflections give full visibility without any moving part to maintain.
judge_comment: A mirrored cavity does not help operation, and it is a safety and arcing concern in a microwave, so the link to the need is weak.

title: Moulded Recyclable Shell
new_elements: Injection-moulded polymer housing (The wrapper is a single moulded shell instead of a stamped steel one.)
rationale: A cheap moulded housing lowers cost, which lets the savings go into simpler controls.
judge_comment: A moulded housing mainly reduces cost, and it reaches the operation need only through an assumed reinvestment in controls.

title: Radiation Leakage Indicator Light
new_elements: Leakage warning strip (A strip on the door changes colour if the seal is compromised, so users know it is safe.)
rationale: A simple colour check gives users confidence in safety without any technical knowledge.
judge_comment: It addresses safety confidence rather than operation, and a reliable leakage-sensing strip is technically doubtful.

title: Passive Heat-Pipe Cooling
new_elements: Heat-pipe fins (Sealed heat pipes carry magnetron heat to outside fins with no fan.)
rationale: No fan means no noise and no dust, so the appliance is quieter and calmer to use.
judge_comment: Passive cooling for a magnetron is hard at the heat loads involved, and it has little to do with operation simplicity.

title: Moulded Mono-Shell Body
new_elements: Moulded composite shell (A single moulded shell with a metal mesh layer replaces stamped steel wrapper.)
rationale: A smooth moulded body has no sharp edges and is easy to lift and clean.
judge_comment: A moulded shell with a mesh layer barely touches operation simplicity, and microwave shielding at the seams would be hard.

title: Light-Diffusing Door Bezel
new_elements: Frosted light-diffusing bezel (A clear bezel with a light pipe lets room light show inside, with no mesh.)
rationale: A clear window is easier to see through and to clean than a mesh.
judge_comment: A mesh-free window is easier to see through, but removing the mesh would leak microwaves, and it has little effect on operation.

title: Cavity Liquid Foam Seal
new_elements: Expanding foam seal (Foam that seals the gap when the door closes and compresses.); Self-sealing foam strip (Strip that seals the gap without alignment.)
rationale: The seal fixes itself on closing, so the user never handles the gasket.
judge_comment: A foam door seal is largely invisible to the user and does not affect operation, and foam would not reliably contain microwaves.

title: Fully Transparent Cavity Glass
new_elements: Electrochromic clear wall (Wall glass that is always clear and needs no internal lamp.)
rationale: Food is always visible without the user having to switch anything on.
judge_comment: Always-clear glass with no lamp is tenuously tied to ease of use, and it's vague, since a cavity with no light can't actually show the food and an electrochromic wall needs power and shielding.

title: Screwless Snap Panels
new_elements: Snap-fit assembly (Panels clip together with no screws or tools.)
rationale: Simple assembly keeps the product plain and uncluttered for the user.
judge_comment: Snap-fit assembly is a common manufacturing technique and does not change how the user operates the oven.

title: Silent Passive Cooling
new_elements: Passive vent grille (Vent that cools the machine by convection with no fan noise.); Silent operation (Runs without fan noise that might cause confusion.)
rationale: A quiet machine gives no confusing sounds to interpret.
judge_comment: Silent passive cooling barely affects ease of operation and is hard to do for a high-power magnetron.

title: Plastic Clamshell Wrapper
new_elements: Moulded polymer clamshell (A lightweight shell with an internal metal screen replaces the steel wrapper and louvres.); Metallised polymer shielding (Conductive coating or mesh provides RF containment inside a plastic shell.)
rationale: A light shell is easy to pick up and move, so the user never needs help.
judge_comment: Metallised plastic shielding is a real substitution, but it does little for simple operation and RF containment and durability are doubtful.

title: Thermoelectric Silent Cooler
new_elements: Thermoelectric cooler pad (A solid-state pad moves heat from electronics to a fin, with no moving parts.)
rationale: No moving parts means no fan to clean or hear, so the appliance feels reassuring.
judge_comment: Thermoelectric cooling is inefficient and costly for magnetron-level heat, and it has little bearing on ease of operation.

title: Fabric Swap-Cover Wrapper
new_elements: Swappable fabric cover (Soft zip-on cover in colours, replacing the steel wrapper.)
rationale: A soft, familiar cover looks and feels friendly instead of technical.
judge_comment: A fabric cover is a cosmetic change that does not make operation simpler, and it raises heat and fire concerns.

title: Snap-Fit Shell
new_elements: Injection-moulded snap shell (A moulded polymer shell with snap-fit joints replaces stamped and welded steel panels.)
rationale: Snap joints mean the casing is cheap to make and easy to keep in shape.
judge_comment: A polymer shell is unrelated to ease of use and has problems with RF shielding and heat.

title: Fold-Flat Oven
new_elements: Foldable shell (The microwave folds flat for storage and unfolds into place without tools.)
rationale: A unit that folds flat is easy to store and set up without needing help.
judge_comment: A foldable shell is novel but impractical given microwave shielding, and it has little connection to ease of operation.

title: Solar Warm Tray
new_elements: Solar-charged battery base (A battery base charged by a solar panel powers the magnetron.); Solar energy harvest (Converts sunlight to stored electricity.)
rationale: Removing the plug removes the need to think about sockets and wiring.
judge_comment: A solar battery cannot supply the power a magnetron needs and does little to make operation simpler.

title: Auto-Adjusting Voltage Core
new_elements: Universal input power converter (Accepts any mains voltage and frequency and converts it safely.)
rationale: The oven works anywhere in the world, so travelling users never face a voltage problem.
judge_comment: Universal voltage handling addresses travel convenience, not learning-free operation, and it is not a real substitution of a simpler part.

title: Fold-Away Oven Chassis
new_elements: Foldable shell (Shell folds flat for storage and unfolds for use, moulded from one polymer piece.)
rationale: A flat-packed oven that folds away suits a student's small room.
judge_comment: Foldable polymer shell targets storage, not ease of operation, and is implausible for a microwave cavity needing rigid metal shielding.

title: Lid Acts as the Plate
new_elements: Dish-as-cavity-floor (The microwave uses whatever dish the user places on it, with no separate tray.)
rationale: Using the user's own dish removes a part that could be lost, misplaced, or misunderstood.
judge_comment: Removing the tray is a plausible substitution, but the idea is unclear (the title mentions a lid), and it does little for the simplicity of operation.

title: Fog-Proof Seal Without Choke
new_elements: Ceramic fiber gasket (Compressed ceramic fiber seals the door without needing a quarter-wave choke.)
rationale: A simpler seal removes the need for users to avoid bumping or misaligning the door.
judge_comment: Ceramic gasket doesn't address operation simplicity and likely can't replace a choke for RF sealing; rationale is weak.

title: Rounded Edge Cavity Mouth
new_elements: Soft-edged cavity mouth (A soft rubber lip around the opening makes the cavity safe to touch and reach.)
rationale: Soft edges make the cavity hard to hurt yourself on, so no caution is needed when loading.
judge_comment: A rubber lip around the opening addresses safety rather than operation, and rubber near microwave heat and seals is questionable.

title: Reflective Mirror Door
new_elements: Mirrored inner glass (Door glass with a metal-free mirror coating to show the inside through reflection.)
rationale: A mirror is a simpler way to check the food than any hole pattern.
judge_comment: A mirror coating on the inner glass doesn't help operation and could interfere with microwave shielding and visibility.

title: Skip-the-Door Heat Pulse
new_elements: Single heat pulse (One fixed pulse of heat that reheats any food with no settings at all.)
rationale: With one fixed pulse there is nothing to choose, so there is nothing to learn.
judge_comment: A single fixed pulse removes choices, but one setting cannot properly heat varied foods, and the 'Skip-the-Door' name and the mechanism are unclear and vague.

title: Zero Stored Charge Design
new_elements: Stores no energy after switch-off (No capacitor holds charge, so nothing needs discharging.)
rationale: Users never worry about a lethal charge, so the machine needs no caution around it.
judge_comment: This is a safety property rather than an operating simplification, and it doesn't say how the design avoids storing charge.

title: Snap-fit recycled shell
new_elements: Snap-fit recycled polymer shell (Outer shell moulded in one piece from recycled polymer, with no stamped steel.)
rationale: A cheap moulded shell lowers cost and weight so the unit is easy to move.
judge_comment: A recycled polymer shell is a cost and weight idea that does not help operation, and a plastic shell is questionable for microwave shielding and heat.

title: Quiet Gravity Vent
new_elements: Rear chimney vent (Warm air rises through a single rear chimney, which needs no louvre design)
rationale: A single vent with no moving air is simpler to understand and safer to place near walls.
judge_comment: A gravity chimney vent is unlikely to cool a magnetron adequately and has little connection to operational simplicity.

title: Molded Shell Housing
new_elements: Conductive polymer molding (A single moulded shell with a conductive coating replaces the stamped steel wrapper and hinges.)
rationale: A single moulded part is cheaper to make and avoids parts that could catch the user's fingers.
judge_comment: A molded conductive shell is a manufacturing change that does little for ease of operation, and shielding and heat performance are doubtful.

title: Low-Voltage Power Brick
new_elements: 24 V SMPS power brick (A low-voltage switched-mode supply replaces the transformer, capacitor and diode stack.)
rationale: Without a lethal charge the user can open the unit at any time with no fear.
judge_comment: A 24 V supply cannot drive a magnetron, which needs kilovolts, so it is physically implausible, and opening the unit has nothing to do with operating it without a learning curve.

title: Fold-Away Stand Mount
new_elements: Wall-mounted folding unit (The unit folds flat and mounts on a wall at a comfortable height.)
rationale: A wall-mounted unit is at a reachable height and frees up counter space.
judge_comment: Wall mounting barely affects operation simplicity and is not really a substitution of a part; microwave ventilation and weight also limit a folding design.

title: Window Mesh Peel-Off
new_elements: Peel-off mesh film (A transparent film with a fine microwave-blocking mesh sticks to the door glass.)
rationale: A film is cheap, can be replaced in seconds, and keeps the door simple.
judge_comment: A peel-off mesh film does not simplify operation and would be unsafe as a microwave shield, since a film is not a reliable replacement for the door's metal mesh.

title: Modular Stackable Cabinet
new_elements: Stackable base unit (A flat base unit stacks under a shelf so the cavity is above the base.)
rationale: A stacking design fits small kitchens without needing counter space.
judge_comment: Stacking saves space but has no bearing on ease of operation, and it substitutes nothing.

title: Snap-Fit Modular Assembly
new_elements: Snap-fit tool-free assembly (Panels snap together with no screws or welds.)
rationale: Simpler assembly cuts cost, so the low-price tier can afford better, simpler controls.
judge_comment: Snap-fit assembly is a manufacturing tweak that has almost no direct link to ease of use.

title: Pulp-Molded Shell
new_elements: Recycled pulp moulding (Casings are moulded from recycled fibre instead of stamped sheet metal.)
rationale: A simple moulded shell is cheap to make and easy to recycle.
judge_comment: A pulp shell cannot provide RF shielding or heat resistance, and it has no bearing on operational simplicity.

title: Low-Voltage RF Stack
new_elements: Low-voltage capacitive RF drive (Drive with no stored high voltage, so nothing is left charged.)
rationale: Removing the stored charge removes the fear of an unplugged appliance still being dangerous.
judge_comment: Vague, and a capacitive drive with no stored high voltage is physically implausible for generating microwave power; it also has little to do with ease of operation.

title: Cavity Sound Sealer
new_elements: Silent operation housing (A sealed housing removes the fan and magnetron hum so cooking is silent.)
rationale: Silent operation removes the need to listen for a signal, so the user just checks the food.
judge_comment: Silent operation barely relates to ease of use, and removing the fan and magnetron hum is technically doubtful, with the audible cue arguably useful.

title: No Stored Charge Design
new_elements: Zero stored high voltage (Energy is never held in a capacitor, so nothing stays charged)
rationale: Users never need to worry about a lethal charge after unplugging.
judge_comment: Zero stored high voltage is vague and barely touches operational simplicity, and the magnetron still needs high voltage, so the claim is questionable.

title: Passive Capacitor Discharge
new_elements: Low-voltage energy buffer (A low-voltage buffer replaces the lethal capacitor, so no charge remains after unplugging.)
rationale: No lethal charge means the user can clean or service the oven without fear.
judge_comment: Addresses safety during servicing rather than operation; a low-voltage buffer cannot realistically replace the high-voltage capacitor in a magnetron circuit.

title: Plug-Free Induction Hob Link
new_elements: Hob-linked power bus (Cable that shares the power of the hob's induction coil.); Powers from the hob (The oven draws power through the hob's connection.)
rationale: A kitchen that is already wired for cooking needs no extra plug or socket.
judge_comment: Powering from an induction hob is implausible, unsafe and does little for operating simplicity.
